lines.japanese: 「……忍、イルカ好きなの？」
lines.english: “...Do you like dolphins, Shinobu?”

lines.japanese: 「んー、昔は嫌いだった。気持ち悪かった」
lines.english: “Hmm. I used to hate them. They creeped me out.”

lines.japanese: 「え、どこが？」
lines.english: “What about them?”

lines.japanese: 「……得体の知れない知性を持ってそうで」
lines.english: “...They seemed to have this eerie, unknowable intelligence.”

lines.japanese: 「ちょっとわかる……イルカって、不思議よね」
lines.english: “I kind of see what you mean... Dolphins are mysterious.”

lines.japanese: 「でも、今はそんなこともないよ。むしろ好きかな」
lines.english: “I don't feel that way anymore. I guess I actually like them now.”

lines.japanese:
「……申し訳ないって感じなのかな。
　昔、嫌っていた分」
lines.english: “...Maybe I feel like I owe them an apology for how much I used to hate them.”

lines.japanese: 「でも、いいの？　自分用だったんじゃないの？」
lines.english: “But are you sure? Wasn't it for you?”

lines.japanese: 「いいんだ。これ見てたら、笛子にあげたくなった」
lines.english: “It's fine. Seeing this one made me want to give it to you.”

lines.japanese: 「それは……嬉しいけど……なんだか悪いわね」
lines.english: “I'd love that... but I'd feel a little bad.”

lines.japanese: 「ご機嫌取りって思ってくれて構わないよ」
lines.english: “You can think of it as me trying to get on your good side.”

lines.japanese: 「…………ありがと。じゃあ、いただくわ」
lines.english: “............Thank you. In that case, I will.”

lines.japanese:
照れくさそうに額をかきながら、笛子は小さく礼
を告げた。
lines.english: Fueko scratched her forehead self-consciously and murmured her thanks.

lines.japanese:
「……あずさ、宝箱見に行くと長いよね。
　一回あけると、絶対全部検分するから」
lines.english: “...Azusa always takes ages when she goes to look at her treasure chest. Once she opens it, she has to inspect every last thing.”

lines.japanese: 「大切なのよ」
lines.english: “They're precious to her.”

lines.japanese:
幼い頃の玩具は、子供にとってただの器物ではな
くなる。
lines.english: A child's old toys cease to be mere objects.

lines.japanese: 「満ち足りてしまうのかな」
lines.english: “Maybe that leaves her feeling content.”

lines.japanese: 「幸せよね、それは」
lines.english: “That sounds like happiness, doesn't it?”

lines.japanese: 「きっとね」
lines.english: “I'm sure.”

lines.japanese:
垂らしていた忍の手に、絡むものがあった。
　笛子の指だ。
lines.english: Something wound itself around Shinobu's lowered hand. Fueko's fingers.

lines.japanese: 「……どうかした？」
lines.english: “...Is something wrong?”

lines.japanese: 「私の幸せ、ここに置いても良かったのかしら」
lines.english: “I wonder if I could have left my happiness here.”

lines.japanese: 「いいに決まってる」
lines.english: “Of course you could.”

lines.japanese:
忍は知っている。
　七人の中、ただ一人笛子だけが……工場にまとま
った私物を置いていない。
lines.english: Shinobu knew. Of the seven, Fueko alone... kept no collection of personal belongings at the factory.

lines.japanese:
あの沙也加でさえ、していることを笛子はしてい
ない。
lines.english: Even Sayaka had done what Fueko had not.

lines.japanese:
椅子、カップ、ブラシ……そういったものだけだ。
　一抹の寂しさはある。
　だとしても、強いることはしない。
lines.english: A chair, a cup, a brush... that was all. There was a touch of loneliness in that. Even so, he would not force her.

lines.japanese:
笛子次第のことだから。
　尊重だけがあり、押しつけはない。
lines.english: The choice was Fueko's. There was only respect, never pressure.

lines.japanese:
そういう関係が最上のものだと、このとき忍はま
だ信じていた。
lines.english: At the time, Shinobu still believed that was the finest kind of relationship.

lines.japanese: 「どうしちゃったの？　悩みでもある？」
lines.english: “What's wrong? Something on your mind?”

lines.japanese: 「……あるのかも」
lines.english: “...Maybe there is.”

lines.japanese: 「聞こうか？」
lines.english: “Want to talk about it?”

lines.japanese: 「話せない……とても……」
lines.english: “I can't tell you... I just can't...”
“I see...”

lines.japanese: 「ごめんなさいね……」
lines.english: “I'm sorry...”

lines.japanese: 「謝ることはないけどね」
lines.english: “You don't need to apologize.”

lines.japanese: 「笛子が話したい時になったら、そうしてよ」
lines.english: “Talk to me whenever you feel ready.”
“...All right.”

lines.japanese:
「家、大変なんだから、誰かに話したい時だってあ
　るさ」
lines.english: “Things are rough at home. Sometimes you must want someone to talk to.”

lines.japanese:
笛子は何も言えなくなる。
　反して指の力は強まり、忍を求めた。
lines.english: Fueko could no longer say a word. But her fingers tightened around his, reaching for him.

lines.japanese: あずさが玩具をいじるかすかな物音さえ感じ取れる。
lines.english: They could hear even the faint sounds of Azusa fiddling with her toys.

lines.japanese: 両者の間に、ただ静寂だけが置かれていた。
lines.english: Only silence lay between them.

lines.japanese: 「むー」
lines.english: “Mmm.”

lines.japanese:
隙間から忍び込んだ冷たさで、忍は夕の訪れを知
った。
lines.english: A chill slipped in through the cracks and told Shinobu that evening had come.

lines.japanese:
薄汚れた携帯用の椅子は、座り心地も悪く、背も
たれもない。
lines.english: The grimy folding chair was uncomfortable and had no back.

lines.japanese:
読書に耽っていて気が付かなかったが、背中が軋
むように痛んだ。
lines.english: Absorbed in his book, he had failed to notice the grinding ache in his back.

lines.japanese:
伸びをして、全身の骨をほぐす。
　若い体は柔軟で、骨の音さえしない。
　二つに折り、よじり、裏に返し……。
lines.english: He stretched, loosening every bone in his body. His young body was supple; not even his joints cracked. Folded double, twisted, turned inside out...

lines.japanese:
さんざん体をいじめてやると、四肢の内に火がと
もったような熱がこもった。
lines.english: By the time he was done putting his body through the wringer, heat glowed in his limbs as though a fire had been lit inside them.

lines.japanese:
痛みはとうに失せていた。
　そうして残ったのは、唯一の気がかり。
lines.english: The pain had long since vanished. Only one concern remained.

lines.japanese: 「……おかしい」
lines.english: “...Something's wrong.”

lines.japanese:
無人の工場で一人、忍は呟く。
　夕刻。
　学校が終わりすぐにここに来た。
lines.english: Shinobu murmured alone in the deserted factory. Evening. He had come straight here after school.

lines.japanese:
以来、ずっと連絡を待っている。
　笛子からの電話は、まだない。
lines.english: He had been waiting for word ever since. Fueko had yet to call.

lines.japanese: 「どうしよう……」
lines.english: “What should I do...?”

lines.japanese:
先ほど、メールも出した。
　しかし返信は来ない。
　どのみち、もう今日は時間もない。
lines.english: He had sent her a message a little while ago. But no reply had come. Either way, there was no time left today.

lines.japanese:
じきに暗くなる。
　約束の勉強も、また後日ということになるだろう。
lines.english: Darkness would fall soon. Their promised study session would have to wait for another day.

lines.japanese:
それはそれで構わないが、連絡がなかったのはな
ぜだろう？
lines.english: That was fine, but why hadn't she contacted him?

lines.japanese:
笛子が約束を違えるとは考えにくかった。
　今一度、電話をしてみる。
　留守番電話サービスに繋がれた。
lines.english: It was hard to imagine Fueko breaking a promise. He tried calling once more. Her voicemail picked up.

lines.japanese: 「……貴宮です。連絡ください」
lines.english: “...This is Atemiya. Please call me.”

lines.japanese: まさか事件にでも巻き込まれたのではなかろうか。
lines.english: Surely she had not been caught up in some kind of incident.

lines.japanese:
ろくでもない考え。
　一度繋がると、癖ができる。
　神経回路も、認識も。
lines.english: A rotten thought. Once a connection formed, it became a habit. Neural pathways and perceptions alike.

lines.japanese:
気が付かない方が幸福な騙し絵も、この現実には
数多いが、さて今回はどうだろう。
lines.english: Reality was full of optical illusions one was happier not seeing through. Was this one of them?

lines.japanese:
椅子に座る気はなくなった。
　何か行動を選択しなければいけない精神状態に陥る。
lines.english: He had no desire to sit down anymore. His state of mind demanded action.

lines.japanese:
しかし留守電まで入れた以上、電話を繰り返して
も意味はない。
lines.english: But now that he had left a message, there was no point in calling again and again.

lines.japanese:
またしつこくかけることで、笛子に煙たがられる
のは避けたかった。
lines.english: He wanted to avoid making a nuisance of himself by calling again and again.

lines.japanese: 本当にそれでは子供の行いだから。
lines.english: That really would be childish.

lines.japanese: 「なら」
lines.english: “Then...”

lines.japanese: 出口のなさに辟易しはじめた頃、電話が鳴った。
lines.english: Just as he was growing sick of having nowhere to turn, the phone rang.

lines.japanese: 一秒かからず通話ボタンを押せた。
lines.english: He hit the answer button in under a second.

lines.japanese: 「もしもし？」
lines.english: “Hello?”

lines.japanese: 『伊月です』
lines.english: “It's Izuki.”

lines.japanese: 多少張りつめてはいたが、落ち着いた声だった。
lines.english: Her voice was somewhat tense, but composed.

lines.japanese:
忍の胸中、乱れていた心の単位が磁力に沿う砂鉄
を思わせて整列していく。
lines.english: Inside Shinobu's chest, the scattered grains of his heart fell into line like iron filings in a magnetic field.

lines.japanese: 「どうしたの？」
lines.english: “What's wrong?”

lines.japanese: 『ごめんなさい……行けなくなっちゃった』
lines.english: “I'm sorry... I won't be able to come.”

lines.japanese: 「それはいいよ。学校の用事？」
lines.english: “That's all right. Something at school?”

lines.japanese: 『うん』
lines.english: “Yes.”

lines.japanese: 「だろうと思ったよ」
lines.english: “I thought so.”

lines.japanese: 『タイミング、悪かったみたい』
lines.english: “Looks like the timing was bad.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、構わない」
lines.english: “That's fine.”

lines.japanese:
「で、今日はもう帰るから、今度にしたいんだけ
　ど……」
lines.english: “I'm heading home now, so I thought we'd leave it for another day...”
“Another time...”

lines.japanese: うろたえた気配が伝わってきた。
lines.english: He could hear her dismay.

lines.japanese: 『そうね……今度よね』
lines.english: “Yes... Another time.”

lines.japanese: 「いつにしよう？」
lines.english: “When should we reschedule?”

lines.japanese: 『ええと……』
lines.english: “Well...”

lines.japanese:
『その、ちょっとまだわからないみたい。
　予定の方が立て込んでいて……
　学校だけじゃなくて、』
lines.english: “Um... I'm not quite sure yet. My schedule is getting rather crowded... And not only with school.”

lines.japanese: 「予定が立たない？」
lines.english: “You can't make any plans?”

lines.japanese: 水を向けると、ほっとした声が、
lines.english: At his prompting, relief entered her voice.

lines.japanese: 『ごめん』
lines.english: “I'm sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「それってさ」
lines.english: “You know...”

lines.japanese: 『なに？』
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese:
「あの本によると、交際お断りの作法そのままの気
　が……」
lines.english: “According to that book, this seems like textbook etiquette for turning somebody down…”

lines.japanese: 『え？　ち、違う！　違うわよ？』
lines.english: “What? N-no! It isn't. It really isn't.”

lines.japanese:
「そうだよね？　なんか、いろいろ途中が抜けてる
　気もするし……」
lines.english: “Right? It does feel as if quite a few steps are missing…”

lines.japanese: 『断ったりはしません』
lines.english: “I'm not turning you down.”

lines.japanese:
軽く怒ったように言う。
　少しメスを入れたい言葉ではあるが、今は置いた。
lines.english: She sounded faintly angry. The wording tempted him to dissect it, but he let it go for now.

lines.japanese: 「で、どうしたって？」
lines.english: “So what happened?”

lines.japanese: 『……実はね、ちょっと厄介事に巻き込まれそうで』
lines.english: “...The truth is, I may be about to get caught up in something complicated.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだって？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 聞き捨てならないセリフ。
lines.english: He couldn't let that pass.

lines.japanese: 「詳しく」
lines.english: “Details.”

lines.japanese:
『……あ、違うの、厄介というか……
　難しいというか』
lines.english: “...No, that's not quite right. Not troublesome so much as... difficult.”

lines.japanese: 『そちらにしてみれば、つまらないこと』
lines.english: “To you, it would probably seem trivial.”

lines.japanese: 「僕には関係ないと？」
lines.english: “Because it has nothing to do with me?”

lines.japanese: 『私個人の人間関係とも絡むことだから』
lines.english: “It also involves some personal relationships of mine.”

lines.japanese: 「……それは、立ち入れない」
lines.english: “...Then I can't pry.”

lines.japanese:
『ごめんなさい。約束も破ってしまったし……
　お詫びしたいんだけど……
　少し忙しくなりそうで』
lines.english: “I'm sorry. I broke our promise... I'd like to make it up to you... but it seems I'm going to be busy for a while.”

lines.japanese: 「仕方ないことだし、そのことはいいよ」
lines.english: “It couldn't be helped, so don't worry about that.”

lines.japanese: 「でも、少し気になる」
lines.english: “But I am a little concerned.”

lines.japanese: 『……ええと……ごめん』
lines.english: “...Um... I'm sorry.”

lines.japanese: 何度目だろうか。
lines.english: How many times had she said that now?

lines.japanese:
女性に何度も謝罪させるようなことを自分は問い
つめているらしい。
lines.english: Apparently he was pressing her hard enough to make her apologize again and again.

lines.japanese:
デートの参考にしたあの本には載っていなかった
ことだが、それはきっと間違いであるのだろう。
lines.english: His dating book had said nothing about this, but it was surely the wrong thing to do.

lines.japanese:
「……次の約束は、しばらく先のことになりそうだ
　ね」
lines.english: “...It sounds like it may be a while before we can make plans again.”

lines.japanese: 『ゆとりができたら、こっちから連絡するから』
lines.english: “I'll contact you once I have some room to breathe.”

lines.japanese: 「了解」
lines.english: “Understood.”

lines.japanese:
互いに軽く息をついて、ひとまず会話を終わらせ
るタイミングを得た。
lines.english: They each breathed a small sigh and, for the moment, found a place to end the conversation.

lines.japanese: 『……じゃあ』
lines.english: “...Well, then.”

lines.japanese: 「ねえ」
lines.english: “Wait.”

lines.japanese:
だというのに、忍の気持ちは一歩、前に出た。
　いや、実は逆だ。
　忍は何も読み取らなかった。
lines.english: And yet Shinobu's feelings took one step forward. No—the truth was just the opposite. Shinobu had read nothing at all.

lines.japanese:
無造作に口を開いただけだった。
　結果として、ベストの形で相手の心を突いたに過
ぎない。
lines.english: He had simply opened his mouth without thinking. As a result, he had struck her heart in exactly the right way.

lines.japanese: 忍は空気を読めなかった。
lines.english: Shinobu could not read the room.

lines.japanese: 「なにかできることはない？」
lines.english: “Isn't there anything I can do?”

lines.japanese:
笛子の呼吸が、停止するのがわかる。
　続く、くぐもった声は、想像以上に深刻なものを
含んだ。
lines.english: He heard Fueko's breath stop. When her muffled voice followed, it carried a gravity far beyond anything he had imagined.

lines.japanese: 『……妹が、いるの』
lines.english: “...I have a little sister.”

lines.japanese: 「知ってる」
lines.english: “I know.”

lines.japanese: 『あの子を、お願いできない？』
lines.english: “Could I ask you to look after her?”
“...What?”

lines.japanese: 「お願いというと……」
lines.english: “When you say look after her...”

lines.japanese: 返答がくるのに、だいぶかかった。
lines.english: It was a long while before she answered.

lines.japanese:
『友達がいないの。だから……いつも一人で……
　まだ言葉を話さないの』
lines.english: “She has no friends. So... she's always alone... and she still doesn't speak.”

lines.japanese: 「…………無口なだけじゃなくて？」
lines.english: “............You don't mean she's simply quiet?”

lines.japanese:
忍の知り合いにも、無口な人間はいた。
　斎と沙也加だ。
　沙也加はもともと言葉自体が少ない。
lines.english: Shinobu knew two quiet people himself. Itsuki and Sayaka. Sayaka simply spoke very little to begin with.

lines.japanese:
人前でみだりに大口を開けることに抵抗があると
かなんとか。
lines.english: Something about disliking opening her mouth too wide in front of people.

lines.japanese:
斎の方は、知り合った頃はわりと口数も普通にあ
ったように記憶していた。
lines.english: As for Itsuki, Shinobu remembered him being reasonably talkative when they first met.

lines.japanese:
だが、ともに過ごす時間が長くなればなるほど、
物静かになっていったものだ。
lines.english: But the longer they spent together, the quieter he became.

lines.japanese: 怪訝に思ったことがあり、葉子に訊ねたことがある。
lines.english: He had once found it curious and asked Youko about it.

lines.japanese:
自宅でも無口だそうだ。
　つまりは、沈黙を好むタイプであったということ。
lines.english: Apparently he was quiet at home too. In other words, he was simply the type who preferred silence.

lines.japanese:
そして真実の関係性に言葉はいらない……といっ
た古いタイプであること、だそうだ。
lines.english: And, so he had been told, the old-fashioned type who believed true bonds had no need of words.

lines.japanese:
しかし笛子の言う『言葉を話さない』は、少し意
味が異なっていた。
lines.english: But Fueko meant something rather different when she said her sister ‘didn't speak.’

lines.japanese: 『……１才や２才じゃないの。もう１０になるわ』
lines.english: “…She isn’t one or two years old. She’ll be ten.”

lines.japanese: 『お医者にもかかった。けど原因はわからないって』
lines.english: “We've taken her to doctors, but they say they don't know the cause.”

lines.japanese:
『理解力は人並みにあるようなの。精神年齢の発達
　には問題がないって。ただ言葉だけが使えないの』
lines.english: “Her comprehension seems normal. They say her mental development isn't impaired. She simply cannot use words.”

lines.japanese:
『文字を読むこともできるし、驚けば悲鳴をあげるの
　に……言葉だけが』
lines.english: “She can read, and she screams when she's startled... It is only words.”

lines.japanese:
『精神は正常。声帯や喉に問題があるわけでもない。
　だから脳になんらかの原因があるんじゃないかっ
　て言われてる……』
lines.english: “Her mind is normal. There is nothing wrong with her vocal cords or throat. So they believe the cause may be somewhere in her brain...”

lines.japanese:
『だからあの子には、友達がいないの。意思の疎通
　ができないから』
lines.english: “That's why she has no friends. She can't communicate.”

lines.japanese: 一息に笛子は話す。
lines.english: Fueko poured it all out in a single breath.

lines.japanese: 「……彼女とは、もう知り合いだから」
lines.english: “...I already know her.”

lines.japanese: 『友達になってあげて、欲しいの』
lines.english: “I want you... to be her friend.”

lines.japanese:
「構わないけど、笛子のかわりに友達になってくれ
　とか言うつもりなら、ごめんだよ」
lines.english: “I don't mind. But if you're asking me to be her friend in your place, then no.”

lines.japanese: 「二人まとめてでないと、受けられないよ」
lines.english: “Only if it includes both of you.”

lines.japanese: 『……うちね、両親が頼りにならないの』
lines.english: “...My parents aren't dependable.”
“What?”

lines.japanese:
『もうあの子が原因で、疲れ果てているの。
　普通の子供じゃないから』
lines.english: “They've been worn out by her. Because she isn't an ordinary child.”

lines.japanese: 『親にも心を開かない。母親も父親も呼ばない』
lines.english: “She won't open her heart even to them. She won't even call them Mother or Father.”

lines.japanese:
『意志は薄弱で、自ら行動しようとしない。泣きも
　しない。応えもしない。食べろと言えば食べる。
　歩けと言えば歩く』
lines.english: “She has almost no will of her own and never tries to act for herself. She doesn't cry. She doesn't respond. Tell her to eat, and she eats. Tell her to walk, and she walks.”

lines.japanese:
『最初こそ大変だったけど、言葉を理解するように
　なって、本当に手がかからない子供になった。機
　械みたいに、ね』
lines.english: “It was difficult at first, but once she learned to understand words, she became a child who required almost no care at all. Like a machine.”

lines.japanese: 『そして近所で評判になって、学校でも噂になって』
lines.english: “People in the neighborhood started talking. Then rumors spread at school.”

lines.japanese:
『……一度、夜になっても帰ってこないことがあって
　近所に知らない人間に車に連れ込まれたって聞いて
　……私は死にものぐるいで捜した……」
lines.english: “…Once, she didn’t come home even after dark. I heard from someone nearby that a stranger had taken her into a car… I searched for her frantically.”

lines.japanese:
『大騒ぎして警察まで呼んで……近所の人たちにお
　願いして……親にも連絡したけどその日は帰って
　こなかった』
lines.english: “I raised an alarm and called the police... begged the neighbors to help... I contacted my parents too, but neither of them came home that day.”

lines.japanese:
『仕事と、男つきの観劇はさぞかし大切だったんで
　しょうね。結局、妹は知り合いの人に見つけても
　らった……』
lines.english: “Their work, and going to the theater with a man, must have been very important. In the end, an acquaintance found my sister...”

lines.japanese:
『変質者だった……結局、未然に防げたんだけど……
　あの子は悲鳴をあげないから！』
lines.english: “It was a predator... In the end, he was stopped before anything happened... but she doesn't scream!”

lines.japanese:
『……自分がされかかったことがわからなかったか
　ら……さぞかし犯人からすれば簡単そうに見えた
　んだろうって』
lines.english: “…She didn’t understand what had nearly been done to her… I suppose she must have seemed such an easy target to the person who took her.”

lines.japanese: 『最後に警察の人にあやまった時、私言われた』
lines.english: “When I apologized to the police at the end, one of them said something to me.”

lines.japanese:
『……人様に迷惑かけるような子供は、首に縄でも
　つけておけって』
lines.english: “...If a child was going to cause other people that much trouble, I ought to keep her on a leash.”

lines.japanese:
『捜索を手伝ってくれた近所の人たちも、そうしな
　かったら対外的にまずいというだけで参加してく
　れたけど……針のむしろだった……』
lines.english: “The neighbors who helped search only joined in because refusing would have looked bad... Every moment with them was agony.”

lines.japanese: 「……人間的な反応だと思うよ。笛子には悪いけど」
lines.english: “...I think that's a very human reaction. I'm sorry, Fueko.”

lines.japanese: 『そうね。他人だものね』
lines.english: “Yes. They're strangers.”

lines.japanese: 『けど親は……他人じゃない。じゃないのにっ』
lines.english: “But my parents... aren't strangers. They aren't!”

lines.japanese: 語尾が嗚咽に乱れかけた。
lines.english: The end of the sentence nearly dissolved into a sob.

lines.japanese:
『……お金持ちのお坊ちゃんと、社会に出たことも
　ない良家の子女の夫婦だから……問題に向き合う
　力を持ってないの。私だけがあの子の味方なの』
lines.english: “...My parents are a pampered rich boy and a sheltered daughter of a good family who has never been out in the world... They don't have the strength to face a problem. I'm the only person on her side.”

lines.japanese:
『……私が忙しくなったら、あの子一人ぼっちにな
　る……』
lines.english: “...If I become busy, she'll be all alone...”

lines.japanese: 「忙しいって、何するの？」
lines.english: “What will keep you so busy?”

lines.japanese: 「自宅にも戻れないようなことなの？」
lines.english: “Is it something that would keep you from coming home?”

lines.japanese: 『……ことによっては、そうなるかも知れない』
lines.english: “...Depending on how things go, it may.”

lines.japanese: 忍の心を、ちくりと何かが刺した。
lines.english: Something gave Shinobu's heart a little stab.

lines.japanese: 「ことによってはって……」
lines.english: “Depending on how things go...?”

lines.japanese:
『うちの両親は離婚はしないと思う。ただ別居はす
　るかも知れない。そしてどちらも、妹を引き取り
　たいとは思っていないと思う』
lines.english: “I don't think my parents will divorce. But they may separate. And I don't think either of them wants custody of my sister.”

lines.japanese:
笛子の声が次第に凛と、覚悟を帯びていくのが、
忍には恐ろしかった。
lines.english: Fueko's voice steadily acquired a firm, resolved edge. Shinobu found it frightening.

lines.japanese: まるで決死の覚悟が、根底にあるように思えて。
lines.english: As though a readiness to die lay beneath it.

lines.japanese: 『だから私は稼がないといけない』
lines.english: “So I have to earn money.”

lines.japanese: 「……笛子が育てるの？」
lines.english: “...You're going to raise her?”

lines.japanese:
『お金は、なんとかなると思うけど……親だってそ
　のあたりは……だけど、どう転ぶかわからないか
　ら……』
lines.english: “I think the money will somehow work out... My parents should at least handle that much... but I don't know how this will end...”

lines.japanese:
『なんとかしないといけない。大学で悠長に勉強し
　ている暇はないように思う』
lines.english: “I have to do something. I don't think I can afford to take my time studying at university.”

lines.japanese:
『だから私の力に価値があるものなら、それを利用
　して一刻も早く自立しないと……そうして、あの
　子をなんとか育てないと……』
lines.english: “If there's any value in what I can do, I have to make use of it and become independent as soon as possible... Then somehow, I have to raise her...”

lines.japanese: 「……しないと、いけない」
lines.english: “You... have to.”
“...What?”

lines.japanese: 「まるで、それが義務であるかのように話すね」
lines.english: “You talk as though it's an obligation.”

lines.japanese: 『それはもちろん……義務じゃない』
lines.english: “Of course... It's my duty.”

lines.japanese: 「気持ちじゃなくて、義務なの？」
lines.english: “Duty, not affection?”

lines.japanese: 「笛子は妹さんのことを……愛しているの？」
lines.english: “Do you... love your sister?”

lines.japanese: 『それは、もちろん家族としては、』
lines.english: “Of course, as family...”

lines.japanese:
「質問を変えるよ。なら妹さんはどう？　笛子のこ
　とを愛していると思う？」
lines.english: “Let me put it another way. What about your sister? Do you think she loves you?”

lines.japanese:
『……どうかしら。少なくとも……話しかけてはく
　れないもの』
lines.english: “...I don't know. At the very least... she never talks to me.”

lines.japanese:
「ならどうして自分は距離を置いて、僕に預けよう
　とするの？」
lines.english: “Then why are you distancing yourself and trying to leave her with me?”

lines.japanese: 『だから、それは……自立しないと……』
lines.english: “Because... I have to become independent...”

lines.japanese:
「ご両親は妹さんは引き取りたくないんでしょ？
　笛子の方はどうなの？」
lines.english: “Your parents don't want custody of her. What about you?”

lines.japanese: 『……父は、母の方に行けって』
lines.english: “...My father told me to go with my mother.”

lines.japanese: 『母は、あなたの好きになさいって』
lines.english: “My mother told me to do whatever I wanted.”

lines.japanese:
「……なるほど。別に望まれているわけじゃないっ
　てこと」
lines.english: “...I see. So neither one particularly wants you.”

lines.japanese: 『顔には出てるわね。面倒だって』
lines.english: “It's written all over their faces. I'm a nuisance.”

lines.japanese:
『自宅の処分って、結構大変なの。私の家も、実際
　のところ祖父名義のものでね。売り払うわけには
　いかない』
lines.english: “Dealing with a house is surprisingly complicated. Ours technically belongs to my grandfather, so they can't simply sell it.”

lines.japanese:
『けど両親とも、ご近所の人間とは会いたくないか
　ら、引っ越したいと考えてる』
lines.english: “But neither of my parents wants to face the neighbors, so they both want to move.”

lines.japanese:
『……私と妹が暮らしたいなら、そう手配してくれ
　るって』
lines.english: “...They said that if my sister and I wanted to live there, they would make the arrangements.”

lines.japanese: 『大黒柱ね』
lines.english: “I'd be the breadwinner.”

lines.japanese: 笑う。無理は、隠せなかった。
lines.english: She laughed. She could not hide the strain.

lines.japanese:
『だからもうすぐにでも、身を立てないといけ
　ないの』
lines.english: “That's why I have to stand on my own as soon as I possibly can.”

lines.japanese:
『……妹を見つけてくれた人がね……とても信頼で
　きる人なんだけど、仕事を斡旋してくれるって。
　私にもできる仕事だって』
lines.english: “…The person who found my sister… is very trustworthy. They offered to arrange a job for me. Something even I could do.”

lines.japanese:
『ただ、時間面で不規則な仕事だから、あまり家に
　はいられないかもってことなの』
lines.english: “But the hours are irregular, so I might not be able to spend much time at home.”

lines.japanese: 「事情はわかった」
lines.english: “I understand the situation.”

lines.japanese:
「……でも笛子、結果として……それは君自身を妹
　さんから遠ざけることになるね」
lines.english: “...But Fueko, in the end... that will only take you farther away from your sister.”

lines.japanese: 『…………だから、あなたに……』
lines.english: “............ That's why I asked you...”

lines.japanese: 「わかった」
lines.english: “All right.”

lines.japanese: 『本当？』
lines.english: “Really?”

lines.japanese: 「ただし、笛子も込みだよ」
lines.english: “Only if you're included too.”

lines.japanese:
『……私、これからはあまり時間取れないかも知れ
　ない……』
lines.english: “...I may not have much time from now on...”

lines.japanese:
「２４時間ってわけでもないんじゃない？　暇な時
　でいいよ。けどこれで関係がないとばかりに無視
　されるのは本意じゃない」
lines.english: “It's not as if you'll be working twenty-four hours a day, right? Come whenever you have time. But I don't want you to ignore us as though none of this had anything to do with you.”

lines.japanese: 『そ、そんなことしませんっ』
lines.english: “I-I would never do that!”

lines.japanese: 「なら、いいね？」
lines.english: “Then we agree?”

lines.japanese: 『……ええ、ありがとう』
lines.english: “...Yes. Thank you.”

lines.japanese:
「ごめんなさいごめんなさいで、やっとありがとう
　か……」
lines.english: “Sorry, sorry—and at last, I get a thank-you out of you…”

lines.japanese:
「本物の言葉を引き出すのは、大変だって思った
　のさ」
lines.english: “I was thinking how hard it is to draw out a real word.”

lines.japanese: 「……まだまだだってことさ。僕がね」
lines.english: “...I've still got a long way to go. Me, I mean.”

lines.japanese:
勉強道具を片づける。
　用意していた回転式の黒板も、奥に引っ込める。
lines.english: He put away the study materials. He moved the revolving blackboard he had prepared back into storage as well.

lines.japanese:
黒板はつい最近になって備わった備品で、この付
近にある不法投棄物の山からの拾いものである。
lines.english: The blackboard was a recent addition, salvaged from a heap of illegally dumped trash nearby.
“...Now then.”

lines.japanese:
工場内を見渡す。
　忍一人しかいない空間は静かで、よそよそしい。
lines.english: He surveyed the factory. With Shinobu its only occupant, the space was silent and distant.

lines.japanese: 他人がいない空間は嫌いではないが、好きでもない。
lines.english: He didn't dislike being alone in an empty place. But he didn't like it either.

lines.japanese:
ならなぜ、友とともにこの場所を作り上げたのか
が、わからない。
lines.english: Then why had he built this place together with his friends? He didn't know.

lines.japanese:
自分のことは謎が多い。
　物心ついてから得た心には、先天的欠陥でもある
のかも知れない。
lines.english: There were many mysteries about himself. Perhaps the heart that had formed once he became aware of himself carried some congenital defect.

lines.japanese: そもそも心として成立しているのかどうか―――
lines.english: Did it even qualify as a heart in the first place—

lines.japanese:
笛子は刺激的だ。
　おおよそ忍の知る限り、もっともバランスの取れ
た人間だろう。
lines.english: Fueko was stimulating company. As far as Shinobu knew, she was probably the most balanced person of all.

lines.japanese:
未熟でもないし、できすぎて鋭すぎることもない。
　時に厳しいが、愛はある。
　そして人並みに悩み、逃げ、苦しむ。
lines.english: She was neither immature nor so exceptionally capable that she became too sharp. At times stern, but loving. And she worried, fled, and suffered like anyone else.

lines.japanese:
まっとうな人格だ。
　周囲の人間について思ってみる。
lines.english: A sound human being. He turned his thoughts to those around him.

lines.japanese:
章二は懐の広い人間だ。
　命をかけて守ることはできるが、しかし手をとり
あってともに苦しむことはない。
lines.english: Shouji was big-hearted. He could stake his life to protect someone, but would never take their hand and suffer beside them.

lines.japanese:
ただ感情の赴くままに先走り、勝手に満足してし
まう。
lines.english: He charged ahead wherever his emotions led him and came away satisfied on his own.

lines.japanese:
そんな人間でも、大元には大切なるものが必要ら
しい。
lines.english: Even someone like that apparently needed something precious at the root of his being.

lines.japanese:
家庭にも学校にも街にもそれを見出せなかった章
二は、忍たちにそれを求めたのだろう。
lines.english: Unable to find it in his family, school, or town, Shouji had probably sought it in Shinobu and the others.

lines.japanese:
あずさは棘を失っている。
　もはやかつてのように、忍に無形の悪意を向ける
ことはないだろう。
lines.english: Azusa had lost her thorns. She would surely never again direct that formless malice toward Shinobu as she once had.

lines.japanese:
それが彼女唯一の個性だったというのに。
　母親から継いだ、否定のしようもないほど選択制
のない、唯一だったのに。
lines.english: And yet it had been her only distinguishing quality. Inherited from her mother, entirely beyond her power to choose, it had undeniably been hers alone.

lines.japanese:
壊してしまった。
　大切にしなければならない。
lines.english: He had destroyed it. Now he would have to treasure her.

lines.japanese:
彼女の新たな物語が完成するよう、努力してやら
ねばならない。
lines.english: He would have to work toward completing her new story.

lines.japanese:
沙也加は樫の木のように真っ直ぐに立つ。
　尊く、高く、孤独にすぎる。
lines.english: Sayaka stood straight as an oak. Noble, tall, and far too solitary.

lines.japanese:
彼女は他者そのものだが、あまりにも完全な他者
性は異質でさえある。
lines.english: She was otherness itself, yet otherness so complete became alien in its own right.

lines.japanese:
斎はもっともシンプルかも知れない。
　非常に協力的でまず同調ありきの態度を、忍には
見せる。
lines.english: Itsuki might be the simplest of them. With Shinobu he was extraordinarily cooperative, always beginning with agreement.

lines.japanese:
使い勝手の良さを感じるが、道具のように扱って
しまうのは問題がありそうだ。
　しかし斎は道具そのものなのだ。
lines.english: His usefulness was palpable, though treating him as a tool seemed problematic. And yet Itsuki was himself a tool.

lines.japanese:
葉子はその名の通り、日々新たなものに触れ、芽
吹いている。
lines.english: True to her name, Youko touched something new each day and put out fresh shoots.

lines.japanese:
いずれ豊かな針葉をつけることを期待しているが、
幸か不幸か奇妙な案配だ。
lines.english: He hoped she would someday grow a wealth of needles, but for better or worse, things had taken a peculiar turn.

lines.japanese:
だが空気のような存在になってしまうよりはまし
だった。
lines.english: Still, it was better than her becoming a presence as insubstantial as air.

lines.japanese:
不器用な人間ばかりだ。
　笛子は貴重だ。
　多く教わる必要がある。
lines.english: They were all clumsy people. Fueko was invaluable. There was much he needed to learn from her.

lines.japanese:
まだまだ、笑いかけてもらわねばならない。
　叱りつけてくれねばならない。
　人間とは何か、教えてもらわねばならない。
lines.english: He still needed her to smile at him again and again. Needed her to scold him. Needed her to teach him what it meant to be human.

lines.japanese:
他のいかなる方法でもなく、ただ肌と空気を挟ん
だ生身のつきあいから。
lines.english: Not through any other medium, but in direct, flesh-and-blood contact, with only skin and air between them.

lines.japanese:
鞄を背負う。
　引き上げるついでに、少し笛子の家まで様子を見
に行こうと考えていた。
lines.english: He shouldered his bag. On his way back, he thought he'd stop by Fueko's house and see how things were.

lines.japanese: 軽い気持ちだった。
lines.english: He gave it little thought.

lines.japanese:
駅前である。
　線路沿いに南下すれば、笛子の家に行くことがで
きる。
lines.english: He was outside the station. Following the tracks south would take him to Fueko's house.

lines.japanese:
およそ忍の知る限り、伊月家と駅を結ぶ最短距離
の始点となるのはこの駅だ。
lines.english: As far as Shinobu knew, this station was the starting point of the shortest route to the Izuki house.

lines.japanese:
続く道が一直線だからだ。
　さもなくば大きく迂回し、陸橋まで使う羽目になる。
lines.english: That was because the road beyond ran perfectly straight. The alternative was a broad detour involving the overpass.

lines.japanese:
自転車などの足を忍はあまり使わない。
　自力で歩くのは、その速度が好きだからだ。
　一時間をかけて４キロを歩く、リズムがだ。
lines.english: Shinobu rarely used a bicycle or any other means of getting around. He liked the pace of walking under his own power. The rhythm of covering four kilometers in an hour.

lines.japanese:
生き急ぐ必要などはない。
　幸い、行動圏は全て徒歩で行き来できる範囲内にあ
ったし、また歩きでなければできないことも数多い。
lines.english: There was no need to rush through life. Fortunately, every part of his world lay within walking distance, and many things could only be done on foot.

lines.japanese:
仲間との通学もその一つだ。
　一時、ともに通学をするため、笛子は一度駅から
忍の家に向かって歩いている。
lines.english: Going to school with his friends was one of them. For a while, when they went to school together, Fueko would first walk from the station to Shinobu's house.

lines.japanese: わざと無駄足を踏んでいるのだ。
lines.english: She deliberately went out of her way.

lines.japanese:
もっとも彼女がいつも、待ち合わせ場所の近くに
ある矢作屋という雑貨屋で、手作りのパンを買い求
めているのを知っている。
lines.english: He did know, however, that she always stopped to buy homemade bread at a general store near their meeting place called Yahagiya.

lines.japanese:
たまに早く行くと、進学校の制服を着た少女が古
びた建物の隣で、しなびたサラリーマンのようにパ
ンをぱくついている姿をよく見た。
lines.english: Sometimes, when he arrived early, he would see a girl in a college-prep school uniform beside the weathered building, wolfing down bread like a worn-out salaryman.

lines.japanese:
ちぐはぐな様子を忍がよく笑ったので、笛子はそ
れ以降、店裏の庭だか荒れ地だかわからないような
場所まで入り、こそこそと隠れて朝食を摂るように
lines.english: Shinobu laughed at the incongruous sight so often that Fueko eventually began sneaking behind the shop, into a place that might have been a garden or a patch of wasteland, and hiding there to

lines.japanese: なってしまった。
lines.english: eat her breakfast.

lines.japanese: ……反省。
lines.english: …A little self-reflection was in order.

lines.japanese: もっとも笛子にしてみれば、
lines.english: From Fueko's point of view, of course—

lines.japanese:
「なんでパン食べてて笑われないといけない
　のよー！？」
lines.english: “Why should I get laughed at just for eating bread?!”

lines.japanese:
ということであり、事実同行するあずさや章二が、
同じ笑い所に反応したことはない。
lines.english: —and in fact, neither Azusa nor Shouji, who accompanied them, had ever found the same thing funny.

lines.japanese:
忍だけが微笑ましく感じたのだ。
　彼らにしてみれば、
lines.english: Shinobu alone found it charming. From their perspective—

lines.japanese: 「笛子だってパンくらい食うだろうぜ」
lines.english: “Fueko eats bread too, you know.”

lines.japanese: であり、
lines.english: —and—
“...What?”

lines.japanese:
であった。
　同じことをあずさがしていたら、
lines.english: —were the only reactions. Had Azusa done the same thing—

lines.japanese:
―――それはそれで微笑ましいものだろうが―――
　違う反応になったはずだ。
lines.english: —charming though it might have been in its own way—the reaction would have been different.

lines.japanese:
あの優等生の笛子が、悪く言えば貧乏臭い方法と
場所でパンを貪り食っている様が、忍にはどうにも
可愛らしいのである。
lines.english: The sight of a model student like Fueko greedily devouring bread in a manner and place that, to put it unkindly, looked downright shabby struck Shinobu as irresistibly adorable.

lines.japanese: 個人差といえばそれまで。
lines.english: One could simply put it down to individual differences.

lines.japanese:
単に忍はそういった差異に敏感で、空気を恣意的
に読み取ることに際だっているということに過ぎない。
lines.english: It simply meant that Shinobu was sensitive to such differences and remarkably good at reading an atmosphere however he pleased.

lines.japanese:
彼は周辺で起こる人間関係の機微を、ほとんど理
解していてもおかしくはない。
lines.english: He might very well understand nearly every subtlety of the human relationships unfolding around him.

lines.japanese:
解釈はそれぞれだろう。
　焦点は、それを態度に出すかどうかなのである。
lines.english: Interpretations would vary. What mattered was whether he allowed that understanding to show.

lines.japanese:
たとえばあずさのことにしてもそうだった。
　あずさの忍に対する気持ちなど、である。
　閑話休題。

ためしに机を一撫ですると、接した布の面が真っ
黒になった。
lines.english: He gave the table an experimental wipe, and the cloth came away pitch-black.
“Ugh.”

lines.japanese:
最初に思ったのは、バケツがいるということ。
　そして思ったより、時間がかかりそうだということ。
lines.english: His first thought was that he needed a bucket. His second was that this would take longer than expected.

lines.japanese:
忍はせっせと働いた。
　何かを忘れるように。
　そう、忘れたかったのだろう。
lines.english: Shinobu worked diligently. As though trying to forget something. Yes. That was probably what he wanted.

lines.japanese:
本当に忘却していたのかも知れない。
　それ以外の何を、できたというのか。
lines.english: Perhaps he had truly forgotten. What else could he have done?

lines.japanese:
無力な人間でしかない忍に、できることはそう多
くはない。
lines.english: There was only so much a powerless human being like Shinobu could do.

lines.japanese:
いつか悲しむ時が来ると、誰も教えてやることは
できない。
lines.english: No one could tell him that the day would come when he would grieve.

lines.japanese:
手を止めて、忍は思う。
　不安事があったはずだ。
lines.english: Shinobu stopped working and thought. There had been something troubling him.

lines.japanese:
空を見る。
　空は青い。
　どこまでも青く、曇りない色。
lines.english: He looked at the sky. The sky was blue. Blue without end, a color untroubled by clouds.

lines.japanese:
忘れている気がした。
　忘却してはならないことを。
lines.english: He felt as though he were forgetting something. Something he must never forget.

lines.japanese:
リビングに座る千鳥の目は、注意深く中庭の忍に
合わせられていた。
lines.english: Chidori sat in the living room, her eyes trained carefully on Shinobu in the courtyard.

lines.japanese:
不器用にテーブルを拭く少年を追う眼球以外、微
動だにしない。
lines.english: Apart from her eyes tracking the boy as he clumsily wiped the table, she did not move a muscle.

lines.japanese:
注視しているようでいて、その実、熟考にふける
様子。
lines.english: She seemed to be watching him, but in truth she appeared lost in deep thought.

lines.japanese: やがて電話を手に取る。
lines.english: At length, she picked up the phone.

lines.japanese: 「……貴宮千鳥です」
lines.english: “...This is Chidori Atemiya.”

lines.japanese:
「すいませんね。
　少しお願いしたいことがありまして」
lines.english: “Sorry to trouble you. There's a small favor I'd like to ask.”

lines.japanese:
千鳥は思いも寄らぬ縁故を持つ。
　いくつかのことを確認し、依頼し、指示を下した。
lines.english: Chidori had connections no one would ever have suspected. She confirmed several matters, made a request, and issued instructions.

lines.japanese: 「よろしくお願いします。ええ、すぐにでも―――」
lines.english: “I appreciate it. Yes, as soon as possible—”

lines.japanese:
電話を切る。
　言葉の通り、彼らはすぐに動いてくれるだろう。
lines.english: She hung up. As she had said, they would surely act at once.

lines.japanese: 「でも、それがあなたのためなのです、忍」
lines.english: “But this is for your own good, Shinobu.”

lines.japanese:
確信という骨格に強められた言葉は、しかしガラ
スの向こうで呑気に掃除をしている忍には届かない。
lines.english: Conviction gave her words a solid spine. But they never reached Shinobu as he cleaned blithely on the other side of the glass.

lines.japanese: 向けられている、強い感情を宿した視線にも。
lines.english: Nor did the gaze fixed upon him, heavy with emotion.

lines.japanese:
庭をいじっていると、塀の外をなんだか見覚えの
ある頭がひょこひょこと横切っていたのだ。
lines.english: While Shinobu worked in the garden, a strangely familiar head bobbed past on the far side of the wall.

lines.japanese:
慣れると、頭で他人を見分けることができるもの
らしい。
lines.english: Apparently, with practice, one learned to recognize people by the tops of their heads.

lines.japanese:
雑巾を畳んで椅子の背にかけ、塀の向こうをのぞ
いて確認すると、裏側から道に出た。
lines.english: He folded the rag over the back of a chair, peered across the wall to make sure, then went out to the road by the rear entrance.

lines.japanese: 「……あれー、笛子がいる」
lines.english: “...Well, look who it is. Fueko.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ハイ」
lines.english: “Oh. Hi.”

lines.japanese: さして驚いた様子もなく、ひらひらと手を振った。
lines.english: Without seeming particularly surprised, she gave him a loose wave.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、もうこんなところまで来ちゃったのね」
lines.english: “Oh, we made it this far already.”

lines.japanese: 「こんなところ歩いてるなんて珍しいね」
lines.english: “It's unusual to see you walking around here.”

lines.japanese: 「遠征」
lines.english: “An expedition.”

lines.japanese: 「……妹がね、散歩したがって」
lines.english: “...My sister wanted to go for a walk.”

lines.japanese: 「妹さん？」
lines.english: “Your sister?”

lines.japanese: そのとき、小さな影が脇を通り過ぎた。
lines.english: At that moment, a small shadow darted past him.

lines.japanese: 「こら！」
lines.english: “Hey!”

lines.japanese: 「え、今の？」
lines.english: “Wait, was that her?”

lines.japanese:
「あ、ごめんなさい、奥に行っちゃったみたい……
　もう、ちっとも落ち着いてなくて」
lines.english: “Oh, sorry. It looks as though she went farther in... Honestly, she never stays still.”

lines.japanese: 「見えなかった……」
lines.english: “I didn't see her...”

lines.japanese: 「一瞬だったわね……」
lines.english: “She was only there for an instant...”

lines.japanese: 二人は顔を見合わせて、笑った。
lines.english: They looked at each other and laughed.

lines.japanese: 「元気あるんだ」
lines.english: “She has a lot of energy.”

lines.japanese: 「いっつも一人でぐるぐる遊んでる」
lines.english: “She's always running around in circles by herself.”

lines.japanese: と肩をすくめた。
lines.english: Fueko shrugged.

lines.japanese: 「可愛いじゃない」
lines.english: “That sounds cute.”

lines.japanese: 「……まぁね」
lines.english: “...I suppose.”

lines.japanese: 「なついているんだかどうだかわからないわ」
lines.english: “I can't tell whether she's warmed up to me or not.”

lines.japanese: 「笛子になつくのは難しい」
lines.english: “You're not exactly easy to warm up to.”

lines.japanese: 「なんてこと言うのよ！」
lines.english: “How could you say that?”

lines.japanese: 「だから君、せめて僕になつきなさいよ」
lines.english: “Then at least you should warm up to me.”

lines.japanese: 「……なんてこと言うのよ」
lines.english: “...How could you say that?”

lines.japanese: 「あがっていく？」
lines.english: “Would you like to come in?”

lines.japanese: 「やめとく。あの子爆弾よ」
lines.english: “Better not. That child is a bomb.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、じゃ三年後くらいにでもまた誘おうか」
lines.english: “Hmm. Then maybe I'll invite you again in about three years.”

lines.japanese: 「あはは、そうして」
lines.english: “Ahaha. Do that.”

lines.japanese: そのとき、忍は一つの可能性に思い至る。
lines.english: At that moment, a possibility occurred to Shinobu.

lines.japanese: 「……もしかして、妹さんを紹介しに？」
lines.english: “...Did you come to introduce me to your sister?”

lines.japanese: 「そのつもりだったんだけど……無理かも……」
lines.english: “That was the plan... but it may be impossible...”

lines.japanese:
どこか近くから子供の存在感だけが伝わってくる。
　姿は見えない。
lines.english: He could sense the presence of a child somewhere nearby. But he could not see her.

lines.japanese: 「……活発なお子さんで」
lines.english: “...She certainly is a lively child.”

lines.japanese: 「フォローありがとう」
lines.english: “Thank you for putting it kindly.”

lines.japanese: 「……あ、遠ざかっていく気配」
lines.english: “...Oh. I can sense her moving farther away.”

lines.japanese: 「こらー！　一人でどこか行かないの」
lines.english: “Hey! Don't wander off by yourself!”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ごめん、回収しなきゃ」
lines.english: “Sorry. I have to go retrieve her.”

lines.japanese: 「おつかれさん」
lines.english: “Good luck.”

lines.japanese:
クラスでの会話に耳を傾けている。
　男女混じった声の連なりは、音素へと分解される
前の、ごろりと意味の塊を残した人音。
lines.english: He listened to the talk around the classroom. The mingled voices of boys and girls reached him as human sound—great lumps of meaning not yet broken down into phonemes.

lines.japanese: 聞くともなしに耳に詰まる。
lines.english: They filled his ears without his trying to listen.

lines.japanese: 「……あいつ、どしたの？」
lines.english: “...What's with him?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、なんか集会だって」
lines.english: “Oh, I heard there's some kind of meetup.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだよ集会って？」
lines.english: “What kind of meetup?”

lines.japanese: 「あいつ不良なんだよね」
lines.english: “He's a delinquent, right?”

lines.japanese: 「うっそ、マジで？」
lines.english: “No way. Seriously?”

lines.japanese: 「街ではいきがってんだって」
lines.english: “I heard he acts big downtown.”

lines.japanese: 「やべ、俺あいつにもろノート借りてるよ」
lines.english: “Crap. I’ve been borrowing his notes.”

lines.japanese:
「俺も借りてる。いんじゃね？
　学校ではぜってー大人しいだろ」
lines.english: “So do I. Who cares? He's always quiet at school.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん、意外なんだな」
lines.english: “Huh. I never would've guessed.”

lines.japanese: 「デビュー最近の話だって」
lines.english: “I heard he only started acting tough recently.”

lines.japanese: 「なんだよ。今からかよ」
lines.english: “Seriously? Starting now?”

lines.japanese: 「おまえ憶えてっかな。伊勢崎っていたべ？」
lines.english: “You remember a guy named Isezaki?”

lines.japanese: 忍の頭が、一センチ浮いた。
lines.english: Shinobu's head rose a centimeter.

lines.japanese:
「……あー、小学の時か？
　え、あいつ戻ってんの？」
lines.english: “...Oh, from elementary school? Wait, he's back?”

lines.japanese:
「年少出たって噂で。実際街いたし。俺見たもん、
　一度。取り巻きいるからすぐわかるぜ。なんかすっ
　げぇヤバそうだった」
lines.english: “Rumor says he got out of juvie. I actually saw him downtown once. You can spot him right away by the guys around him. He looked seriously dangerous.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、行かねーし……駅らへんは」
lines.english: “Yeah, well, I don't go near the station...”

lines.japanese: 「彼女作れ」
lines.english: “Get a girlfriend.”

lines.japanese: 「うるせぇなぁ」
lines.english: “Shut up.”

lines.japanese: 「で、どうやばいって？」
lines.english: “So what kind of dangerous are we talking?”

lines.japanese:
「うん。けっこうマジ入ってる感じだった。
　ヤンキーっつうの？　そんな感じ」
lines.english: “Yeah. He looked pretty serious about it. A real delinquent, you know? That kind of guy.”

lines.japanese: 「乱パとかじゃないってこと？」
lines.english: “So not just sex parties or something?”

lines.japanese: 「みたいな。武闘派？　それっぽい」
lines.english: “Looks that way. More of a fighting crowd.”

lines.japanese: 「うわっ」
lines.english: “Whoa.”

lines.japanese:
そして両者の会話は、そのまま別の話題に移り変
わっていった。
lines.english: Then their conversation simply drifted to another subject.

lines.japanese:
伊勢崎宗多―――
　その名前は忍を複雑にする。
lines.english: Souta Isezaki—the name left Shinobu conflicted.

lines.japanese:
葛藤は脳を刺激し、決して好ましいばかりではな
い結果を引き出す。
lines.english: That conflict stimulated his brain, with results that were by no means all welcome.

lines.japanese:
端的に言えば、忍は伊勢崎宗多にいじめられてい
た―――というわけではなかった。
lines.english: Put simply, Souta Isezaki had bullied Shinobu—except that was not what had happened.

lines.japanese:
むしろ忍が宗多を利用していたとも言える。
　彼は腹を立てる理由を持っている、と忍は知って
いた。
lines.english: If anything, Shinobu had made use of Souta. Shinobu knew the boy had every reason to be angry with him.

lines.japanese:
自分を憎む動機としても充分すぎるほどに。
　しかしだからといって、野放図にそれが実行され
ては困る。
lines.english: More than enough reason to hate him. But that didn't mean Shinobu could let him act on it unchecked.

lines.japanese:
宗多という少年は、ただ忍一人を痛めつけて満足
する少年ではないからだ。
lines.english: Souta was not the kind of boy who would be satisfied merely by hurting Shinobu.

lines.japanese:
被害が仲間に及ぶとなれば、忍も黙ってはいられ
ない。
lines.english: If the harm threatened to spread to his friends, Shinobu could not stay silent.

lines.japanese: 指を噛んだ。
lines.english: He bit his finger.

lines.japanese:
自分一人を守ることに比べ、あちらこちらに点在
する仲間を気に掛けるというのは、なんと難しいこ
となのだろう。
lines.english: Compared with protecting only himself, keeping watch over friends scattered here and there was terribly difficult.

lines.japanese:
樋口章二に頼ってはどうかと、最初は考えた。
　だが、と思い直す。
lines.english: At first he thought of relying on Shouji Higuchi. Then thought better of it.

lines.japanese:
例えば行政はその抑止力を傘のように広げ見せる
ことで犯罪を未然に防ごうとする。
lines.english: A government, for example, displays its deterrent power like an umbrella, hoping to stop crimes before they happen.

lines.japanese:
決して万能ではない。
　犯罪に走る直前の人間を、そうと知っていてもお
いそれと処罰できるものではないからだ。
lines.english: That power is never absolute. Even knowing that someone is on the verge of committing a crime, the state cannot readily punish them.

lines.japanese: ましてや、人の心を覗く手段さえないとなれば、だ。
lines.english: All the more so when it has no means of peering into the human heart.

lines.japanese:
官憲は罪の重さで人を正しく保つ。
　正常な心の人間に、それは特に作用する。
　そうでなくとも、ある程度は有功なものである。
lines.english: The authorities keep people in line through the weight of punishment. It works best on those of sound mind. Even on others, it works to a degree.

lines.japanese:
異質な人間といえども我が身は大切だ。
　―――ほとんどは。
lines.english: Even someone outside the norm values their own skin. Most of them, anyway.

lines.japanese:
抑止力が完全ではないことを、国家の安全を司る
者たちは知っている。
lines.english: Those responsible for national security know that deterrence is imperfect.

lines.japanese:
現実を知っている。
　そして……ある究極的な部分で、１００％確実に
全ての人民を守れないとも知っている。
lines.english: They know reality. And... in the final analysis, they know they cannot protect every citizen with absolute certainty.

lines.japanese:
忍は、１００％確実に守らねばならない。
　抑止力ではなく、強制力でなければならない。
　樋口章二は宗多に致命傷を加えることはない。
lines.english: Shinobu had to protect them with absolute certainty. He needed compulsion, not deterrence. Shouji Higuchi would never fatally wound Souta.

lines.japanese:
あの合理的な少年は、追い払うまでは能動的に実
行するが、原因そのものを取り去ってしまおうとは
思わないはずだ。
lines.english: Rational as he was, Shouji would act to drive Souta away, but he was unlikely to want to eliminate the cause itself.

lines.japanese: 樋口章二の優しさと甘さに、忍は落涙しそうになる。
lines.english: Shouji Higuchi's kindness—his softness—nearly brought Shinobu to tears.

lines.japanese:
自分とはまったく違うその姿勢に、惚れ込んだの
だった。
lines.english: That attitude, so utterly unlike his own, was what had made him admire Shouji so deeply.

lines.japanese:
知り合ったのは、共通の友人がいたからだ。
　偶然だった。
　友達になろうと思っていたわけではない。
lines.english: They had met through a mutual friend. By chance. Shinobu had not set out to become friends with him.

lines.japanese:
気が付けば、つるんでいた。
　ある意味、忍の本当の友人は章二だけだ。
lines.english: Before he knew it, they were always together. In one sense, Shouji was Shinobu's only true friend.

lines.japanese:
決断をもって定めたものが友ではないと言うので
あれば、章二は勝手についてきただけだからだ。
lines.english: If friendship was not something established by deliberate decision, Shouji had simply tagged along without permission.

lines.japanese:
そう……彼もまた、守護の対象だ。
　繊細な息遣いを側に感じて、忍は顔を上げた。
lines.english: Yes... he too was someone to protect. At the sound of delicate breathing beside him, Shinobu looked up.

lines.japanese: 「……やあ、どうしたの？」
lines.english: “...Hey. What's wrong?”

lines.japanese:
答えず、少女は冷淡とも受け取れる眼差しを忍に
向ける。
lines.english: Without answering, the girl turned on Shinobu a gaze that might have been mistaken for coldness.

lines.japanese:
その内に秘されたおおよそ１％以下の情愛を模し
たものを、忍だけが知る。
lines.english: Shinobu alone knew of the tiny trace of something resembling affection hidden within it—one percent or less.

lines.japanese:
独特の距離。
　両の指先を、三つ指を今は机のはしにかけていた。
　どこかあどけない、殺意。
lines.english: A peculiar distance. Three fingers of each hand now hooked over the edge of his desk. An oddly innocent murderous intent.

lines.japanese: そう、殺意―――
lines.english: Yes, murderous intent—

lines.japanese: 「いいんだ、沙也加」
lines.english: “It's all right, Sayaka.”

lines.japanese: 響き渡らぬよう、小声で名を呼ぶ。
lines.english: He spoke her name softly, careful not to let it carry.

lines.japanese: 「でもアレは、」
lines.english: “But that thing...”

lines.japanese: 伊勢崎宗多は、
lines.english: Souta Isezaki—

lines.japanese: 「……鋭く、矮小よ」
lines.english: “...is sharp and small.”

lines.japanese: 的確な評価ではなかろうか。
lines.english: Perhaps an accurate assessment.

lines.japanese:
「いや、彼は無差別じゃない。
　ピンポイントで来るよ。何かするとしても」
lines.english: “No. He isn't indiscriminate. If he does anything, he'll come for a very specific target.”

lines.japanese:
「……かなり合理的な人間だ。目の前に立って刺激
　した時だけ、過激に反応する」
lines.english: “…He’s quite rational. He only reacts violently when someone stands in front of him and provokes him.”

lines.japanese: 「向こうから現れる可能性もあるわ。アレの方から」
lines.english: “That thing might come to us on its own.”

lines.japanese: 「逃げるさ」
lines.english: “We'll run.”

lines.japanese: 「……解決にはならないでしょう」
lines.english: “...That won't solve anything.”

lines.japanese:
「私があなたの部下だったら、あなたにさっさと命
　じるよう告げるわ」
lines.english: “If I were your subordinate, I would tell you to hurry up and give the order.”

lines.japanese: 忍は笑った。
lines.english: Shinobu laughed.

lines.japanese: 「部下じゃない、それ」
lines.english: “That's not how subordinates work.”

lines.japanese: 「何か考えでも？」
lines.english: “Do you have something in mind?”

lines.japanese: 「確認してからでないと、なんともね」
lines.english: “I can't say until I've confirmed a few things.”

lines.japanese:
「忍……まさか、あなたはまたアレを玩具にしたい
　の？」
lines.english: “Shinobu... You don't mean to turn that thing into your plaything again, do you?”

lines.japanese: 「誤解を招くような言い方を……」
lines.english: “You could phrase that a little less suggestively...”
“What?”

lines.japanese:
「玩具って。何、沙也加も葉子みたいにそういうの
　好きなわけ？」
lines.english: “Calling him a toy. What, are you into that kind of thing too, like Youko?”

lines.japanese: 「なに、を」
lines.english: “Into... what?”

lines.japanese: 解して、淡く変色した。
lines.english: She understood, and a faint flush rose to her face.

lines.japanese: 「…………ごめん冗談」
lines.english: “............ Sorry. Bad joke.”

lines.japanese:
かぎ状に曲げられた指が忍の鼻をもぎ取ろうとす
る直前に、詫びを入れた。弱かった。
lines.english: He apologized just before her hooked fingers could tear off his nose. He was weak.

lines.japanese:
さすがに教室での“お茶目”は一気に評判になり
そうできつい。
lines.english: That kind of “playfulness” in the classroom would have everyone talking in an instant. He could do without it.

lines.japanese:
「……まあ章二と沙也加は平気だと思うよ。
　強い人間はわかるでしょ」
lines.english: “...I think you and Shouji will be fine. He knows who's strong.”

lines.japanese:
「斎と葉子もまず平気。
　門倉に手を出すほどバカじゃないさ」
lines.english: “Itsuki and Youko should be safe too. He's not stupid enough to pick a fight with the Kadokuras.”

lines.japanese: 「バカではなくても無謀なこともあるけれど」
lines.english: “Even someone who isn't stupid can still be reckless.”

lines.japanese:
「かもね。ただまず心配なのは、一際弱いあずさと
　……あと笛子だ」
lines.english: “Maybe. The ones I'm most worried about are Azusa, who's especially vulnerable, and... Fueko.”

lines.japanese: 最後の瞬間だけは、声も落ち込んだ。
lines.english: Only at the very end did his voice sink.

lines.japanese: 「……笛子は」
「住所も学校も、一番遠いからね」
lines.english: “Her home and school are the farthest away.”

lines.japanese:
心配そうに揺れる瞳。
　忍の不手際を非難する色が確かにある。
　口に出そうか、出すまいか悩んでいる顔だった。
lines.english: Her eyes wavered with concern. They held an unmistakable accusation: Shinobu had mishandled things. Her face said she was debating whether to voice it.

lines.japanese: 「沙也加、それにこれは僕の仕事だ。責任持つさ」
lines.english: “Besides, Sayaka, this is my job. I'll take responsibility.”

lines.japanese: 「そう思うのなら、心配させないで」
lines.english: “If you believe that, don't make me worry.”

lines.japanese: 怒られた。
lines.english: He'd been scolded.

lines.japanese:
「まあ、たとえ多少痛めつけられても守ってみせま
　すよ」
lines.english: “Even if I take a bit of a beating, I'll protect them.”

lines.japanese:
沙也加の眉が乱れた。
　そこで鈴が鳴る。
　生徒らがそれぞれ席に戻っていく。
lines.english: Sayaka's brows drew together. Then the bell rang. The students returned to their seats.

lines.japanese:
沙也加も立ち去る。
　その際、忍の髪の毛を一本抜いた。
lines.english: Sayaka left too. On her way, she plucked a single hair from Shinobu's head.

lines.japanese: 「いたっ」
lines.english: “Ow!”

lines.japanese:
狼藉は誰の目にも止まらなかった。
　ただ忍の発した小さな叫びに、隣席の生徒が少し
顔を向けたくらい。
lines.english: No one noticed the outrage. Only Shinobu's small cry made the student at the next desk glance his way.

lines.japanese: 「おい、聞いたか？」
lines.english: “Hey, did you hear?”

lines.japanese:
廊下に出るなり、声をかけられた。
　章二は壁際に背を預けて、忍を待っていたようだ。
lines.english: The moment he stepped into the corridor, someone called to him. Shouji was leaning against the wall, apparently waiting for him.

lines.japanese: 「……伊勢崎宗多のこと？」
lines.english: “...About Souta Isezaki?”

lines.japanese: 「早いな。それだ」
lines.english: “That was fast. Yeah.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえ、どうするつもりだ？」
lines.english: “What are you planning to do?”

lines.japanese: 「どうもしないよ。今はまだ」
lines.english: “Nothing. Not yet.”

lines.japanese: 「……こっちで手を打てるぜ？」
lines.english: “...I could take care of it.”

lines.japanese: 「打ってもらっちゃ困る」
lines.english: “I'd rather you didn't.”

lines.japanese: 「あん？　どういうことだ？」
lines.english: “Huh? What's that supposed to mean?”

lines.japanese: 「下手に刺激しない方がいい。トイレ行こう」
lines.english: “Better not to provoke him carelessly. Let's go to the bathroom.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ」
lines.english: “All right.”

lines.japanese: 二人は並んで歩き出す。
lines.english: They set off side by side.

lines.japanese: 「釘くらい刺しておいた方がいいんじゃないのか？」
lines.english: “Shouldn't we at least warn him off?”

lines.japanese:
「……向こうの意図がわからない。なぜ戻ってきた
　のか……は地元だからだろうけど」
lines.english: “...We don't know what he intends. As for why he came back... well, this is his hometown.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなにこっちに気を向けるかなって思って」
lines.english: “I just wonder if he'll really pay us that much attention.”

lines.japanese: 「あいつはおまえに恨み骨髄だと思うが」
lines.english: “I'd say that guy holds one hell of a grudge against you.”

lines.japanese: 「忘れているかも知れない」
lines.english: “Maybe he's forgotten.”

lines.japanese: 「……本気じゃないな」
lines.english: “...You don't believe that.”
“Well...”

lines.japanese:
「正直なところ、こっちからつつくより向こうの出
　方待ちがいいと思ってる」
lines.english: “Honestly, I think it's better to wait and see what he does than go poking at him ourselves.”

lines.japanese:
「危険なのはあずさと笛子だけだよ。密に連絡を取
　っていれば、いきなりってことはないと思う」
lines.english: “The only ones at risk are Azusa and Fueko. If we stay in close contact, I don't think anything will happen without warning.”

lines.japanese: 「……そうだな。だがよ」
lines.english: “...True. But...”

lines.japanese:
「わかってる。
　最悪の時は、手段は選ばないようにする」
lines.english: “I know. If the worst happens, I won't rule anything out.”

lines.japanese: 二人はトイレに入った。
lines.english: They went into the bathroom.

lines.japanese: 一緒に出てきた。
lines.english: They emerged together.

lines.japanese: 「オレにも連絡忘れるな。噛ませろ」
lines.english: “Don’t forget to call me too. Let me in on it.”

lines.japanese: 「わかってるとは思うけど、さ」
lines.english: “I'm sure you understand, but...”

lines.japanese:
「こちらから仕掛けるなってことだろ。
　わかったぜ。けど現場判断はするぜ？」
lines.english: “Don't make the first move, right? Got it. But I'll make the call on the ground.”

lines.japanese: 「それは頼むよ」
lines.english: “I'm counting on you.”

lines.japanese: 「しかし、わからんな」
lines.english: “Still, I don't get it.”
“...What?”

lines.japanese: 「おまえがそこまで甘い理由だよ」
lines.english: “Why you're going this easy on him.”

lines.japanese: 「殴られても苦笑いして我慢しておくといいよ」
lines.english: “Even if he hits me, I'll just grin and bear it.”

lines.japanese: 「日本かよ」
lines.english: “What are you, Japan?”

lines.japanese: 「結果として、あちこち敵に回しても」
lines.english: “Even if it means making enemies on every side.”

lines.japanese: ぐ、と拳を握った。
lines.english: He clenched his fist.

lines.japanese: 「……いや、そうなってるぞ、日本……」
lines.english: “...That already happened to Japan...”

lines.japanese:
「……昔のおまえだったら、今頃武器の調達につい
　て考えてるとこだ」
lines.english: “...The old you would be thinking about how to procure weapons by now.”

lines.japanese: 「君はどういう人間像を僕に当てはめているのかね」
lines.english: “What kind of person do you take me for?”

lines.japanese:
「子供の頃、斎とあずさと四人でベイシュートの
　大会に出ただろう」
lines.english: “Remember when the four of us—you, me, Itsuki, and Azusa—entered that Bey Shoot tournament as kids?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ……懐かしい、すごく懐かしい」
lines.english: “Oh... now that takes me back. Really takes me back.”

lines.japanese:
「あの時、対戦相手の手にシュートを直撃させて棄権
　させた時、おまえは『これで一人目潰した』と呟い
　た」
lines.english: “You launched your top straight into your opponent's hand and forced him to withdraw. Then you muttered, ‘That's the first one down.’”

lines.japanese: 「……今の僕なら呟かない」
lines.english: “...The person I am now wouldn't mutter it.”

lines.japanese: 「そういう問題じゃない」
lines.english: “That isn't the issue.”

lines.japanese: 「……まあ、あったかな、そんなこと」
lines.english: “...Maybe something like that happened.”

lines.japanese:
「おまえは途中の過程がスッパリ抜けてる。
　おまえがやるくらいならオレがやった方がはるか
　に穏便なんだがな」
lines.english: “You skip straight over all the steps in between. If one of us has to do something, it'll be a hell of a lot more peaceful if it's me.”

lines.japanese:
「それだと中途半端なんだよ。やるならとことん最
　後までやらないと駄目だ」
lines.english: “That would only leave things half-done. If you're going to do it, you have to see it through to the very end.”

lines.japanese: 「……おいおい」
lines.english: “...Come on.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、やらないけどね」
lines.english: “Not that I plan to do anything.”

lines.japanese: 「だといいがな」
lines.english: “Let's hope not.”

lines.japanese: 「……荒事は任せてもらいたいもんだが」
lines.english: “...I'd still rather you left the rough stuff to me.”

lines.japanese:
後頭部に両手を組んで、章二は自分の教室に戻っ
ていった。
lines.english: Shouji laced his fingers behind his head and returned to his classroom.

lines.japanese: 「それより……問題は他にあるんだ……」
lines.english: “More importantly... there's another problem...”

lines.japanese:
囁きはただ外気を経由して自らの耳にだけ届けら
れた。
lines.english: The whisper passed through the open air to no ears but his own.

lines.japanese:
宗多を牽制する意味はない。
　行動するとしたら、それは笛子に対してのものと
なるだろう。
lines.english: There was no point warning Souta off. If Shinobu took action, it would probably be directed at Fueko.

lines.japanese: なぜなら彼女は、恐らくは忍を裏切るのだから。
lines.english: Because in all likelihood, she would betray Shinobu.

lines.japanese:
ああ、今の顔は誰にも見られたくないなと思った。
　こんな顔は、本当に。
lines.english: Ah. He did not want anyone to see his face just then. Not when it looked like this. Not at all.

lines.japanese:
いざとなった時のことについて、考えるのは億劫
だった。
lines.english: He couldn't be bothered to think about what he would do when the moment came.

lines.japanese: ひどく残酷な自分がそこに立っている気がして。
lines.english: He could almost see a monstrously cruel version of himself standing there.

lines.japanese: 小さな影が横切る―――
lines.english: A small shadow crossed their path—

lines.japanese:
虚ろな形と空疎な輪郭は、邂逅を果たした。
　周囲の人々の努力さえかいくぐり。
　遠い世界から戻ったかのような、顔でだ。
lines.english: An empty form and a hollow outline met. They had slipped past even the efforts of the people around them. Their faces looked as though they had returned from a distant world.

lines.japanese:
星は重力を持つ。
　巨大な天体も、質量と形態に見合った重力を持つ。
lines.english: A star has gravity. A vast celestial body, too, has gravity in keeping with its mass and shape.

lines.japanese:
人もまた小さな質量ではあるが、引き寄せる力を
持つ。
lines.english: Human beings, for all their slight mass, also have the power to draw things to themselves.

lines.japanese:
とりわけ強いのは物理現象ではなく、心的機能に
誘引されるものである。
lines.english: The strongest attraction is not a physical phenomenon at all, but one induced by the workings of the mind.

lines.japanese:
さて。
　心によって人は人を選別する。
　いや、峻別すると言ってもいい。
lines.english: Now then. People use their hearts to sort one another. Or rather, to draw sharp distinctions.

lines.japanese:
嫌いな人間と、好ましい人間。
　好悪の分離に決定的な物理の差はあるのだろうか？
lines.english: People one hates and people one likes. Is there any decisive physical difference between attraction and aversion?

lines.japanese:
そして好き同士が互いに接近することは……果た
して物理的な解析というメスを受け付けるのだろうか。
lines.english: And when two people who like each other draw closer... can that movement truly submit to the scalpel of physical analysis?

lines.japanese:
わからない、と結ぶのは容易い。
　しかしそれでは、耳障りの良い嘘をつくことになる。
lines.english: It would be easy to conclude, “I don’t know.” But that would be to tell a pleasant-sounding lie.

lines.japanese:
人が人を好むのは、何か原因があるのである。
　そして数値化することも、あるいは―――できて
しまう。
lines.english: There is a reason one person likes another. And perhaps it can even—be quantified.

lines.japanese:
誰もが恐れる。
　誰もが隠す。
lines.english: Everyone fears it. Everyone hides it.

lines.japanese:
しかし見えてしまったものは、いかんともしがたい
　伊月笛子は貴宮忍と、会った。
lines.english: But once something has been seen, there is no help for it. Fueko Izuki met Shinobu Atemiya.

lines.japanese:
工場に来たのは、忍が最初だった。
　本棚に触れ、次いですみに追いやられたガラクタ
のいくつかに触れた。
lines.english: Shinobu had been the first to arrive at the factory. He ran a hand over a bookshelf, then over several pieces of junk shoved into a corner.

lines.japanese:
その中には共同で購入したマッサージ機が、一度
も使われることなく安置されていた。
lines.english: Among them, enshrined and never once used, was a massage machine they had all bought together.

lines.japanese:
かぶった埃がなんとなく許容できない。
　触れた。
lines.english: Somehow, he couldn't tolerate the dust coating it. He touched it.

lines.japanese:
想像以上に埃が舞った。
　それで忍は諦めて、そして、
　途方に暮れた。
lines.english: Far more dust rose than he'd expected. Shinobu gave up. And then—stood there at a loss.

lines.japanese: 「……誰も、いないや」
lines.english: “...No one's here.”

lines.japanese:
まだ昼間だった。
　この室内は空のうつろいを取り込みにくいが、そ
れでも落日の遠さだけはわかる。
lines.english: It was still daytime. The room let little of the changing sky inside, but even here he could tell sunset was still a long way off.

lines.japanese:
埃のせいか斜光が目視できる。
　斜めに突き立つ陽光の石英を眺めていると、笛子
がやってきた。
lines.english: Perhaps because of the dust, the slanting light was visible. He was watching quartz shafts of sunlight drive diagonally through the room when Fueko arrived.

lines.japanese: 小さな影をともなって。
lines.english: A small shadow came with her.

lines.japanese:
幼い影は、駆け回っていた。
　寂れた工場という場所は、この年代には冒険島に
等しい魅力を持つ。
lines.english: The young shadow ran about. To a child of that age, an abandoned factory held all the appeal of an adventure island.

lines.japanese:
最初は忍らの周囲を控えめに歩いていたが、今は
敷地中をのべつまくなし走り回っている。
lines.english: At first she had walked timidly around the two of them, but now she raced ceaselessly across the entire grounds.

lines.japanese:
一方、忍と笛子は対峙していた。
　言葉の必要性を感じない瞬間が、両者に訪れていた。
lines.english: Meanwhile, Shinobu and Fueko faced each other. A moment had come when neither felt any need for words.

lines.japanese:
人には時折、そんなことがある。
　言いたいことがあればあるほど、適切な言葉が見
つからないということが。
lines.english: Such moments sometimes came to people. The more one had to say, the harder it became to find the right words.

lines.japanese:
よくよく検討してみれば、実は言うべきことなど
ないことも多い。
lines.english: Often, if one thought it through, there was nothing that needed saying after all.

lines.japanese: （それでも、何か……）
lines.english: (Even so, something...)

lines.japanese: 忍はいろいろなことを思った。
lines.english: Shinobu thought of many things.

lines.japanese:
妹さんのこと。
　伊勢崎宗多のこと。
　笛子自身のこと。
lines.english: Her sister. Souta Isezaki. Fueko herself.

lines.japanese:
うち、重要な項目はどれなのだろうか。
　考えた。
　そして見た。
lines.english: Which of them mattered? He considered it. Then he looked.

lines.japanese:
その日、笛子は美しい。
　憂いだ。
　滲み出る。
lines.english: Fueko was beautiful that day. Melancholy. Seeping through.

lines.japanese:
言葉を失うと、美への理解が変化する。
　より鋭敏にわかる。
　切り口が変わる。
lines.english: When words disappear, one's understanding of beauty changes. It grows sharper. One sees it from a different angle.

lines.japanese: それで忍は本当に理解した。
lines.english: And so Shinobu truly understood.

lines.japanese: 「そうか。僕は君の、外見が好きだったんだ」
lines.english: “I see. It was the way you looked that I liked.”

lines.japanese:
笛子がぽかんと、忍の眉間あたりを見つめた。
　この解、心を数値化しても変わるまい。
　読み取ったものなのだから、間違いがない。
lines.english: Fueko stared blankly at a point somewhere between Shinobu's brows. Even if the heart could be quantified, this answer would not change. He had read the answer in himself; there could be no mistake.

lines.japanese:
外見が好き。
　では中身は？
　笛子に嘆かれてもおかしくはないことを言った。
lines.english: He liked her looks. What, then, of what lay within? He had said something she could hardly be blamed for taking badly.

lines.japanese:
しかし、彼女は微笑んだ。
　この上なく嬉しげに。
　安堵、だったのだ。
lines.english: But she smiled. Utterly delighted. It was relief.

lines.japanese:
影はいつの間にやら、その姿を消していた。
　遠く去ったか、あるいは―――
lines.english: At some point, the shadow had disappeared. Perhaps it had gone far away. Or perhaps—

lines.japanese: 「ねえ」
lines.english: “Hey.”

lines.japanese: 掠れる声が告げる。
lines.english: Her voice came out hoarse.

lines.japanese: 「耳掃除してあげる、約束」
lines.english: “I promised... I'd clean your ears.”

lines.japanese: 真綿のような音色で。
lines.english: Her tone was soft as cotton.

lines.japanese: かくて、耳掃除―――
lines.english: And so—the ear cleaning—

lines.japanese:
鼓膜という脆弱性を他者にさらすこの行為は、そ
うだアレだ……歯医者に似ている、と忍は感じた。
lines.english: Exposing his eardrum—something so vulnerable—to another person reminded Shinobu of... yes, the dentist.

lines.japanese:
正直、怖い。
　敵意がない限り、心地よい時間であるのは間違い
ない。
lines.english: It was honestly frightening. But in the absence of hostile intent, it was undoubtedly pleasant.

lines.japanese:
もし笛子がその気になれば、最小の労力で自分は
殺されてしまう。
lines.english: If Fueko chose to, she could kill him with next to no effort.

lines.japanese: 生死の境目だ。
lines.english: He lay on the boundary between life and death.

lines.japanese:
そこに柔らかな太ももの感触、反対側の耳に添え
られた手の優しさ、耳の内を細い枝の掻痒……この
三つが加わると、あらがえないものが生まれてくる。
lines.english: Then there was the softness of her thighs, the gentle hand cupped over his other ear, and the slender twig stirring an itch inside this one... Together they made something impossible to resist.

lines.japanese:
心臓が不自然に緊張していた。
　いわば、アメとムチの同時。
lines.english: His heart was unnaturally tense. The carrot and the stick at once, so to speak.

lines.japanese:
そんなプレイってあるのかしらん、と忍は愚劣な
疑問を抱いた。
lines.english: Shinobu found himself wondering, idiotically, whether that counted as some kind of play.

lines.japanese:
しかし最も愚劣なのは、反対側を向いてしまいた
いという欲求だろう。
lines.english: But surely the most idiotic thing was his desire to turn and face the other way.

lines.japanese:
桃源郷の類が見つかりそうな気がした。
　でも、たぶんものすごい罪を背負う。
lines.english: He had a feeling some kind of earthly paradise awaited him there. But it would probably be a terrible sin.

lines.japanese: 口を開かず、黙々と作業に励む笛子だ。
lines.english: Fueko continued her work in silence.

lines.japanese: 「ねえ」
lines.english: “Hey.”

lines.japanese: 耳奥をこそぐカリカリという物音が、一瞬止まる。
lines.english: The faint scraping in the depths of his ear stopped for an instant.

lines.japanese: 「……本当はね」
lines.english: “...The truth is...”

lines.japanese: 「笛子に謝らないといけないことがあったんだ」
lines.english: “There's something I need to apologize to you for.”

lines.japanese: 「好きに、理由をつけたくなかった」
lines.english: “I didn’t want to attach a reason to liking you.”

lines.japanese: 「理由のない好きでいたかった」
lines.english: “I wanted to like you for no reason at all.”

lines.japanese: 「それがもっとも尊いことだと、みんなが言うから」
lines.english: “Because everyone says liking someone for no reason is the noblest thing of all.”

lines.japanese: 「でも……僕はそんな自由な人じゃなかったよ」
lines.english: “But... I wasn't free in that way.”

lines.japanese: カリカリコリコリ。
lines.english: Scritch, scrape.

lines.japanese:
乾いた音。
　心の乱れも感じさせない、笛子の触れる音。
lines.english: A dry sound. The sound of Fueko’s touch, giving no hint of agitation.

lines.japanese: 「ごめんよ」
lines.english: “I'm sorry.”

lines.japanese:
手が止まる。
　笛子の皮膚の向こうから届く、艶めかしいような
体内の音。
lines.english: Her hand stopped. From beyond Fueko's skin came the almost sensual sounds inside her living body.

lines.japanese:
血液の流れる様子だろうか。
　あるいは細胞の奏でる、小さな声だろうか。
lines.english: Blood flowing, perhaps. Or the tiny voices of her cells.

lines.japanese: 「六人は、別の六人でもあり得た」
lines.english: “The six of you could have been six different people.”

lines.japanese: そう決めさえすれば。
lines.english: If only he had chosen that way.

lines.japanese:
「だから君が……僕のもとから離れてしまうのは、
　仕方ないって思ってる」
lines.english: “So I think it can't be helped... if you leave me.”

lines.japanese:
否定はない。
　かまわず忍は続けた。
lines.english: She did not deny it. Shinobu went on anyway.

lines.japanese:
頭がスッキリしているうちに、言ってしまいたか
