lines.english: Her shoulders gave a start.

lines.japanese:
「深くは問いつめないけど、自分がいるせいで狙わ
　れていると思ったわけ？」
lines.english: “I won't press you too hard, but did you think they were targeting us because you were here?”

lines.japanese:
やがて観念したのか、少女は活気を帯びることの
ない、しかし誠実な声で、
lines.english: At last, perhaps resigned to it, the girl spoke. Her voice was lifeless, but sincere nonetheless:

lines.japanese: 「……そうよ」
「じゃ伊勢崎宗多のことは知ってるんだね」
lines.english: “Then you know Souta Isezaki.”

lines.japanese:
「驚くことはないよ。あいつとは、子供のころにい
　ろいろ因縁があったんだ」
lines.english: “There's no need to be surprised. He and I had quite a history when we were children.”

lines.japanese: 「そういう話は、本人から聞かなかったの？」
lines.english: “Didn't he ever tell you about that himself?”

lines.japanese: 「……噂くらいは知っていたけど……詳しくは……」
lines.english: “...I'd heard rumors... but I didn't know the details...”

lines.japanese: 「笛子はどこで知り合ったの？」
lines.english: “Where did you meet him, Fueko?”

lines.japanese: 「子供の頃からの知り合いだった」
lines.english: “I'd known him since we were children.”
“...I see.”

lines.japanese: 考え込む。
lines.english: He fell into thought.

lines.japanese: 「幼なじみとか？」
lines.english: “Were you childhood friends?”

lines.japanese:
「ではないけど……もともとは姉が知り合いだった
　の。伊勢崎君が問題を起こして、それで学校を移
　らないといけなくなった時に、私もその場にいて」
lines.english: “Not exactly... My sister knew him first. When Isezaki got into trouble and had to change schools, I happened to be there.”

lines.japanese: 「子供の頃は、よく一緒にいたの」
lines.english: “We spent a lot of time together as children.”

lines.japanese: 「…………なるほど」
「じゃ、伊勢崎宗多が僕を嫌っていることとか……」
lines.english: “So you knew that Souta Isezaki hated me...?”

lines.japanese:
「なんとなくは。でも実際に何かするとは思わなく
　て……」
lines.english: “I had a vague idea. But I never thought he'd actually do anything...”

lines.japanese: 「私が、こちら側にいたせいかも知れないって」
lines.english: “I thought it might be because I was on your side.”

lines.japanese: 「……うーん」
「だから私が向こうにつけば……」
lines.english: “So if I went back over to his side...”

lines.japanese: 「それはどうかな」
lines.english: “I don't know about that.”
“What?”

lines.japanese:
「僕らと伊勢崎宗多の確執はね、そんなものじゃな
　いんだ」
lines.english: “The bad blood between us and Souta Isezaki isn't about something like that.”

lines.japanese: 「子供の縄張り争いだったんだよ」
lines.english: “It started as a children's turf war.”

lines.japanese:
「僕だって、あいつにはひどいことをした。
　尊厳を踏みにじるような真似だってしたんだ」
lines.english: “I did terrible things to him too. I even did things that trampled on his dignity.”

lines.japanese: 「……信じられないわよ」
lines.english: “...I find that hard to believe.”

lines.japanese: 「笛子だって知ってるはずだよ。昔の僕のこと」
lines.english: “You must know what I was like back then, Fueko.”
“...Is that really true?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ。その転校だって、僕のせいだ」
lines.english: “Yes. Even his transfer was my doing.”

lines.japanese: 「まさか」
lines.english: “It couldn't have been.”

lines.japanese: 「彼はね、逃げたんだ」
lines.english: “He ran away.”

lines.japanese:
「僕にてひどくやられて……あれはもうイジメなん
　てものじゃない。侮辱、虐待……いや、そんな言
　葉で説明できるほどシンプルなものじゃない」
lines.english: “After the terrible things I did to him... It had gone far beyond bullying. Humiliation. Abuse... No, it wasn't simple enough to explain with words like those.”

lines.japanese:
「今でもね、いや、今だからこそ……僕は当時の
　自分を恥ずかしく思ってる」
lines.english: “Even now—no, especially now... I'm ashamed of the person I was then.”

lines.japanese: 「……人の所行じゃないと思ってる」
lines.english: “...I don't think what I did was human.”

lines.japanese: 「想像つかないわね、彼の性格からすると」
lines.english: “That's hard to imagine, given what he's like.”

lines.japanese: 「だから、怒りも大きい」
lines.english: “That's why his anger runs so deep.”

lines.japanese:
「英気を養って戻ってきたんだ。学校にも行ってない
　らしいじゃないか。なら失うものなんて何もない」
lines.english: “He built his strength back up and returned. I hear he isn't even going to school. That means he has nothing left to lose.”

lines.japanese:
「……性格が変わってなければ、何でもするんじゃ
　ないかな。今日みたいに」
lines.english: “...If his personality hasn't changed, I imagine he'd do anything. Just like he did today.”

lines.japanese: 「…………でも……宗ちゃんは……」

一番正直なのは心臓だった。
　親しげな呼び方に竦みあがった。
lines.english: His heart was the most honest thing about him. It clenched at how familiarly she said the name.

lines.japanese:
笛子は忍に一片の敵意も向けていない。ただ伊勢
崎宗多のことを呼んだだけなのに。
lines.english: Fueko had not directed the slightest hostility at Shinobu. She had merely spoken Souta Isezaki's name.

lines.japanese: 「……今日も、いたよ」
lines.english: “...He was there today, too.”

lines.japanese: 「……そう、そうだったの」
lines.english: “...I see. So he was there.”

lines.japanese: 「これは僕ひとりのことじゃない」
lines.english: “This isn't only about me.”

lines.japanese:
「あずさや沙也加、葉子のことだってある。そして
　向こうがそう望むなら、回避だって難しい」
lines.english: “Azusa, Sayaka, and Youko are caught up in it, too. And if that's what they want, we won't be able to avoid them easily.”

lines.japanese: 「……バラバラになってたら、駄目なんだ」
lines.english: “...We can't let ourselves be scattered.”

lines.japanese:
「じゃどうするの？　みんな集めて、ほとぼりが冷
　めるまであの工場に住む？」
lines.english: “Then what will you do? Gather everyone together and live in that factory until this blows over?”

lines.japanese: 「……半分、そうしようと思ってたんだ、実は」
lines.english: “...To tell you the truth, I was half considering it.”

lines.japanese:
「何よりも優先しようとしたら、そうする以外にな
　くなる」
lines.english: “If I make this my first priority, there won't be any other choice.”

lines.japanese:
悄然と肩を落とす忍を、笛子は感情の置き所を見
失った者の顔で眺めた。
lines.english: Fueko watched Shinobu's shoulders slump, looking as though she no longer knew what to do with her feelings.

lines.japanese: 「……忍は、いつだってそうだったけど……」
lines.english: “...You've always been like this, Shinobu, but...”

lines.japanese: 「壊したくないものだから、これは」
lines.english: “Because this is something I don't want to see destroyed.”

lines.japanese:
「いろいろなものから、守りたいと思うよ。たった
　一つのものを守れるのだったら、どんな代償だっ
　て支払ってもいい」
lines.english: “I want to protect it from everything. If I could protect just this one thing, I'd pay any price.”

lines.japanese:
「……考えることがありすぎてつらくとも、何もな
　いよりはマシだ」
lines.english: “...However painful it is to have so much to think about, it's better than having nothing.”

lines.japanese: 「何者でもないことは、本当に恐いよ」
lines.english: “Being nobody is truly terrifying.”

lines.japanese:
「どんな人間にだって友達は必要だ。あのまま……
　一人ぼっちに育ったらと思うとぞっとする」
lines.english: “Everyone needs friends. The thought of what I might have become... if I'd gone on growing up all alone chills me.”

lines.japanese: 「でも忍」
lines.english: “But Shinobu—”

lines.japanese:
「そんなに大切なものを持つってことは、失う可能
　性だってあるわけでしょう？」
lines.english: “If you have something that precious, then isn't there always the chance that you'll lose it?”

lines.japanese: 「その重みに、あなた耐えられるの？」
lines.english: “Could you bear that weight?”

lines.japanese: 「……失うことは考えてない」
lines.english: “...I’m not thinking about losing it.”

lines.japanese:
「今はそうでも、絶対に助けられない状況になった
　ら？」
lines.english: “That may be true now, but what if you find yourself in a situation where saving them is absolutely impossible?”

lines.japanese:
「今日はなんとかなった。でも明日は？　学校に行
　っている時に、ひとりの人間が狙われたら？　ど
　うにもならないことって、いくらでもあると思う」
lines.english: “You managed today. But what about tomorrow? What if someone is targeted while you’re at school? I think there are any number of things you can’t do anything about.”

lines.japanese:
「……どうにもならないことについては、よく考え
　てる」
lines.english: “...I think a lot about the things I can't do anything about.”

lines.japanese: 「結論は出た？」
lines.english: “Have you found an answer?”

lines.japanese: 首を振る。
lines.english: He shook his head.

lines.japanese: 「出なかったよ、いつも」
lines.english: “I never have.”

lines.japanese:
「なら……私、やっぱりもうあなたたちと一緒には
　いられない」
lines.english: “Then... I really can't be with all of you anymore.”

lines.japanese:
虚偽も気負いもない言葉に忍は打たれる。
　その中に一片含まれる、かすかな怯えには気付か
ない。
lines.english: The words, free of falsehood or bravado, struck Shinobu. He failed to notice the single faint thread of fear woven through them.

lines.japanese:
長年のつきあい。育んだ何かは、わずか一枚の障
壁に阻まれて霧消してしまうほど、脆く儚いものだ
ったのだろうか。
lines.english: The years they had spent together—had whatever they had nurtured truly been so frail and fleeting that a single thin barrier could make it vanish into mist?

lines.japanese:
実のところ、忍は絆だけが世のあらゆる摂理から
神聖不可侵に反故されるなどとは、微塵も思わない。
lines.english: In truth, Shinobu had never imagined that bonds alone were sacred and stood outside every law that governed the world.

lines.japanese:
努力を失えば、たちまちのうちに形を失い、無価
値な砂塵となって霧散する。
lines.english: The moment the effort ceased, they lost their form and scattered into worthless dust.

lines.japanese:
そんな代物であると理解している。
　世に称揚される愛。
　人々はあまりにも無条件に信奉してしまう。
lines.english: He understood that this was their nature. Love, extolled by the world. People worshiped it far too unconditionally.

lines.japanese:
その怖さや冷たさや無常の様を、見もせずに。
　情愛は守らねばならぬ。
　それを尊いと自覚し、聖別し、奉る必要がある。
lines.english: Without ever seeing its terror, its coldness, or its impermanence. Affection had to be protected. One had to recognize it as precious, consecrate it, and revere it.

lines.japanese:
内を省みる必要もなく、笛子は大切だ。
　だが大切であるが故にどうしても彼女を尊重して
しまう。
lines.english: He needed no soul-searching to know that Fueko was precious to him. Yet precisely because she was precious, he could not help but respect her wishes.

lines.japanese: 奪って、ものにしてしまうべきなのに―――
lines.english: When he ought to seize her and make her his—

lines.japanese: 「それでも、僕は笛子が好きだよ」
lines.english: “Even so, I like you, Fueko.”

lines.japanese:
笛子は撃たれたように立ち尽くした。
　双眸が剥き出しにされ、人形を思わせる表情で忍
を見据えた。
lines.english: Fueko stood frozen as though she had been shot. She stared at Shinobu, eyes wide and naked in a doll-like face.

lines.japanese: 普段の反応とは違う。
lines.english: It was nothing like her usual reaction.

lines.japanese:
怒りがなかった。
　羞恥がなかった。
lines.english: There was no anger. No shame.

lines.japanese:
喜びがなかった。
　悲しみがなかった。
lines.english: No joy. No sorrow.

lines.japanese: やがて―――
lines.english: And then—
“Ha—”

lines.japanese: 短く、笛子は笑った。
lines.english: Fueko gave a short laugh.

lines.japanese:
「アッハハハハハハハハハハハハハハハハハハハハ
　ハハハハハハハハハハハハハハハはハハハハハハ
　ハハハハハハはハハハハハハハハハハハハハ！！」
lines.english: “Ahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahaha hahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahaha hahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahaha!!”

lines.japanese: 翌日から、伊月笛子は忍の前から姿を消した。
lines.english: From the next day onward, Shinobu saw no more of Fueko Izuki.

lines.japanese:
伊月笛子が忍たちの前に姿を見せないようになっ
て、数日が過ぎた。
lines.english: Several days had passed since Fueko Izuki last showed her face to Shinobu and the others.

lines.japanese:
森で忍らを襲った伊勢崎宗多らは、それ以来特に
目立った行動を起こしていない。
lines.english: Since their attack in the woods, Souta Isezaki and his people had done nothing particularly conspicuous.

lines.japanese:
忍たちも仲間内で連絡を回し、工場には行かない
ようにした。
lines.english: Shinobu and his friends spread the word among themselves and stayed away from the factory.

lines.japanese:
樋口章二は牽制のため、学校を休んでいろいろと
行動している。
lines.english: Shouji Higuchi had been missing school while taking various measures to keep their adversaries in check.

lines.japanese: 朝の通学から、二人が欠けた。
lines.english: Two people were missing from the morning walk to school.

lines.japanese:
幸い学校回りに、伊勢崎宗多らが姿を見せること
はなかった。
lines.english: Fortunately, Souta Isezaki and his people had not appeared anywhere around the school.

lines.japanese:
笛子が不在であることが他の仲間をガードしやす
くしているという事実は、確かにあった。
lines.english: There was no denying that Fueko's absence made it easier to guard the rest of the group.

lines.japanese:
位置的に孤立した場所に住んでおり、異なる学校
に通う笛子だ。
lines.english: Fueko lived in an area set apart from the others and attended a different school.

lines.japanese:
忍と斎は、自分の周囲にだけ気を払っていれば良
かった。
lines.english: Shinobu and Itsuki only had to keep watch over their own immediate surroundings.

lines.japanese: 緊迫を保ちつつも、何事もない日々が過ぎていく。
lines.english: The days passed uneventfully, though the tension never lifted.

lines.japanese:
電話は通じない。
　何度コールしても繋がらないし、メールの返信も
ない。
lines.english: He could not reach her by phone. No matter how many times he called, she never answered, and she never replied to his messages.

lines.japanese:
自宅の本電話にもかけてみたが、忍の言葉は留守
電に虚しく吸い取られた。
lines.english: He had tried the house phone as well, only for the answering machine to swallow his words.

lines.japanese: 「……出ないか」
lines.english: “...Still no answer.”

lines.japanese:
何度、こうして電話をかけたことだろう。
　避けられるのは仕方ない。
　ただ安全を確認したかった。
lines.english: How many times had he called like this now? He could accept that she was avoiding him. He only wanted to know that she was safe.

lines.japanese:
わずかでもいいし、事務的な対応だって構わない。
　無事だということを知らせて欲しかった。
lines.english: Even a few perfunctory words would do. He only wanted her to tell him she was all right.

lines.japanese:
諦める。
　ベッドに身を沈ませる。
lines.english: He gave up. He sank onto the bed.

lines.japanese:
「……このまま
　……散り散りに、なってしまうのかな」
lines.english: “...Are we all going ...to drift apart like this?”

lines.japanese:
まさかと思い、次にはその可能性の高さに戦慄が
走る。
lines.english: Surely not, he thought—then shuddered at how likely it seemed.

lines.japanese:
確かに忍たちは聖域を追われた。
　仲間が欠けた。
　会う機会も激減した。
lines.english: They had, undeniably, been driven from their sanctuary. One of their number was missing. Their chances to meet had dwindled.

lines.japanese:
現状が長期に渡って維持されたら？
　起こりうることだ。
lines.english: What if things stayed this way for a long time? It was entirely possible.

lines.japanese: 一分後。
lines.english: One minute later.

lines.japanese:
また電話をかけた。
　もちろん繋がらなかった。
lines.english: He called again. Of course, there was still no answer.

lines.japanese: 伊月笛子は逃げていた。
lines.english: Fueko Izuki was on the run.

lines.japanese:
目立ちたくはなかった。
　追手が自分を見つけやすくなるから。
lines.english: She did not want to draw attention. It would make it easier for her pursuers to find her.

lines.japanese:
しかし走らないわけにはいかず、街中で過度の注
目を受けた。
lines.english: But she had no choice but to run, drawing far too much attention as she raced through town.

lines.japanese:
たとえ追手が自分の顔を知らずとも、疾走する女
生徒を目撃すればピンと来るだろう。
lines.english: Even if her pursuers did not know her face, the sight of a schoolgirl sprinting through the streets would surely tip them off.

lines.japanese: 身を隠さなければならない。
lines.english: She had to hide.

lines.japanese:
最初、笛子はデパートに入った。
　だがすぐ、不穏な気配を感じ取った。
lines.english: First, Fueko ducked into a department store. But she immediately sensed danger.

lines.japanese:
食料品売り場には不釣り合いな、革ジャンの若者
を確認して、すぐに外に出た。
lines.english: She spotted a young man in a leather jacket who looked out of place in the grocery section, and left at once.

lines.japanese: まけはしなかっただろう。
lines.english: She doubted she had shaken them.

lines.japanese:
背中から強いプレッシャーが押しつけられている。
　どこに逃げるか。
lines.english: She could feel an intense pressure bearing down on her from behind. Where could she run?

lines.japanese:
喫茶店などの飲食店はまずい。
　出口が複数なければ袋の鼠だ。
　白昼、車に引き込まれることもある。
lines.english: A café or restaurant would be no good. With only one exit, she would be trapped like a rat. They might drag her into a car in broad daylight.

lines.japanese:
いずれにせよ、車で横付けされる車道沿いは危険
であった。
lines.english: Any road where a car could pull up beside her was dangerous.

lines.japanese: 自宅はどうだろう。
lines.english: What about home?

lines.japanese:
天井裏のロフト空間がある。
　素人には存在すらわからない。
lines.english: There was a loft above the ceiling. An amateur would never even know it existed.

lines.japanese:
あそこに隠れてしまえば……自分一人だったら数
日は―――
lines.english: If she hid up there... alone, she could hold out for several days—

lines.japanese: 「ダメよ……」
頭を振る。
lines.english: She shook her head.

lines.japanese:
妹の存在を、なぜ忘れてしまうのだろう。
　大事な妹だ。
lines.english: How could she have forgotten about her sister? Her precious little sister.

lines.japanese:
両親のいない今、笛子が守ってやらなければなら
ない。
lines.english: With their parents not around, Fueko had to protect her.

lines.japanese: 自宅に戻るのは選択肢から消えた。
lines.english: Returning home was no longer an option.

lines.japanese:
冷静に考えれば、もう張り込まれていることだっ
てあり得る。
lines.english: On reflection, the house might already be under watch.

lines.japanese: 相手は複数。
lines.english: There were several of them.

lines.japanese:
チンピラとはいえ、組織だっている。
　どんな悪知恵を働かせるかわからない。
lines.english: They might be thugs, but they were organized. There was no telling what dirty tricks they might try.

lines.japanese: 絶望が視界を暗くした。
lines.english: Despair darkened her vision.

lines.japanese:
瞬時に悪意に転じたそれは、無形の憎悪となって
世間に照射された。
lines.english: In an instant, that despair turned to malice—a shapeless hatred projected onto the world.

lines.japanese:
だが対象のない憎悪は、拡散して無と同化してい
った。
lines.english: But hatred with no object dispersed and dissolved into nothingness.

lines.japanese:
足が止まる。
　疲れていた。
lines.english: She stopped. She was tired.

lines.japanese: 終わりにしても良かった。
lines.english: She could let it end.

lines.japanese: 頼る相手もいない。
lines.english: There was no one she could turn to.
“...Shinobu...”

lines.japanese:
少年の顔を思い浮かべた。
　ただそれだけで救われたような気持ちになったが、
すぐに幻想は砕ける。
lines.english: She pictured the boy's face. The thought alone made her feel as though she had been saved, but the illusion shattered at once.

lines.japanese: 「頼って、どうするのよ……」
lines.english: “What good would it do to rely on him...?”

lines.japanese: 両方の目頭を、手のふちで押さえる。
lines.english: She pressed the edges of her hands against the inner corners of her eyes.

lines.japanese: 「頼って、どうしてもらうつもりなのよ……」
lines.english: “And if I did, what would I expect him to do...?”

lines.japanese:
そうしなければ泣き出しそうだった。
　逃げ場がないのは現実だけのことではない。
lines.english: Otherwise, she felt she might begin to cry. It wasn't only in the real world that she had nowhere to run.

lines.japanese:
心も同様に閉ざされ追いつめられ、笛子は身動き
が取れなくなる。
lines.english: Her heart, too, was closed off and cornered. Fueko could no longer move.

lines.japanese:
忍に依存し自分は考えることなく、結果だけを受
け入れることはできそうな気がした。
lines.english: It felt as though she could depend on Shinobu, stop thinking for herself, and simply accept whatever came of it.

lines.japanese: だがそれで、伊月笛子はおしまいだ。
lines.english: But that would be the end of Fueko Izuki.

lines.japanese:
壊したくない。
　頼りたい。
lines.english: She did not want to destroy it. She wanted to rely on him.

lines.japanese: 相反する二つの思いがぶつかりあう。
lines.english: The two opposing desires collided inside her.

lines.japanese: いずれを選ぶこともできず、同じ結論に落とされる。
lines.english: Unable to choose either one, she was forced back to the same conclusion.

lines.japanese: 「あはは……」
lines.english: “Ahaha...”

lines.japanese:
力無く笑う。
　自分というものがわからなくなる。
lines.english: Her laugh had no strength in it. She no longer understood what she was.

lines.japanese:
ただ苦悩のしこりだけが、心の中心に埋められて
いて、どうにも気持ち悪い。
lines.english: Only a lump of anguish remained, buried at the center of her heart, and it made her sick.

lines.japanese: まるで癌細胞だ、と笛子は思った。
lines.english: It was like a cancer cell, Fueko thought.

lines.japanese: 「……そうだ、工場」
lines.english: “...That's right. The factory.”

lines.japanese:
顔を上げる。
　身を隠すのに、あれほどうってつけの場所はない。
lines.english: She raised her head. There could be no better place to hide.

lines.japanese: 「あとで、考えよう」
lines.english: “I'll think about it later.”

lines.japanese:
手元の現金も少ない。
　工場には食料の備蓄があったはずだ。
lines.english: She had little cash left. There should be a stockpile of food at the factory.

hyperlinks.preview: It was Shinobu's idea. At first, it was no more than a secret hideout, furnished with whatever odds

japaneseHyperlinks.preview: It was Shinobu's idea. At first, it was no more than a secret hideout, furnished with whatever odds

lines.japanese:
少々拝借して、別の使われていない建物に隠れて
もいい。
lines.english: She could help herself to a little, then hide in one of the other unused buildings.

lines.japanese:
毛布やその他の生活用品もあった。
　なにしろ秘密基地なのだから。
lines.english: There were blankets and other necessities, too. It was a secret base, after all.

lines.japanese:
仲間を裏切るようで少し心が咎めたが、冷徹さを
奮い起こして切り捨てた。
lines.english: The thought that she was betraying her friends pricked at her conscience, but she summoned a cold resolve and cast the thought aside.

lines.japanese: 笛子の前に、少年が二人立ちはだかった。
lines.english: Two boys stepped into Fueko's path.

lines.japanese: 「こいつ？」
lines.english: “This her?”

lines.japanese: 「だな」
lines.english: “Yep.”

lines.japanese:
笛子にしか聞こえない音を立て、気力が萎んでい
った。
lines.english: With a sound only Fueko could hear, her resolve deflated.

lines.japanese: 「はい、これで挟み撃ち」
lines.english: “And now we've got you surrounded.”

lines.japanese: 冗談めかした口調で、背後に二人が立った。
lines.english: Two more stood behind her, one of them speaking as if it were a joke.

lines.japanese: 「伊月笛子ちゃんだっけ？　挟まれちゃったね」
lines.english: “You're Fueko Izuki, right? Looks like you're boxed in.”

lines.japanese: 「とりあえず来てくれる？」
lines.english: “For now, would you mind coming with us?”

lines.japanese:
腰を抱かれた。
　気が弱い少女は、肩を抱かれると腰が引ける。
lines.english: An arm closed around her waist. A timid girl held by the shoulders would instinctively pull back at the hips.

lines.japanese:
そうならないよう、馴れ馴れしく手を回して、逃
げられないよう腰を抱いたのだ。
lines.english: To prevent that, he had casually slipped an arm around her waist and held her so she could not escape.

lines.japanese:
別のひとりが、ハザードを出して道路脇に寄って
きた車の後部ドアを開けた。
lines.english: Another opened the rear door of a car that had pulled to the curb with its hazard lights blinking.

lines.japanese:
そこに押し込まれる状況が、他人事としか思えな
かった。
lines.english: Being shoved into the car felt like something happening to someone else.

lines.japanese:
ただ、溶けそうだった。
　水につけられ、泡が立ち、そして―――
lines.english: She felt herself dissolving. As though immersed in water, bubbles rising, and then—

lines.japanese: なにものでもなくなる。
lines.english: She would become nothing at all.

lines.japanese:
ガラスを隔てて庭を望むリビングだが、今はカー
テンが閉められ、視界を完全に遮断していた。
lines.english: The living room looked out through the glass onto the garden, but now the curtains were drawn, completely shutting off the view.

lines.japanese:
シンと静まりかえった住宅街が、ことさら生命感
覚を喪失させ、忍は世にただ一人佇んでいるかのよ
うな虚無の類に襲われている。
lines.english: The utter silence of the neighborhood drained the world of any sense of life, and a kind of void descended on Shinobu, as though he stood utterly alone in the world.

lines.japanese:
こうして次の手を打てず、変質者よろしく塀の外
にへばりついて３０分。
lines.english: Unable to make his next move, he had spent thirty minutes clinging to the outside of the wall like some kind of creep.

lines.japanese:
ベルを押してしまえばふんぎりもつくが、なかな
か実行には移せない。
lines.english: Ringing the bell would settle the matter, but he could not bring himself to do it.

lines.japanese:
こちらの存在を、室内の笛子に気取られたが最後、
警戒が強められるのではないかという予想。
lines.english: He imagined that if Fueko realized he was outside, she would only become more guarded.

lines.japanese:
かといってすでに彼女は引きこもっている。
　今以上の警戒があるものかどうか。
lines.english: Yet she had already shut herself away. Could she possibly become more guarded than this?

lines.japanese:
理性ではわかっていても、数字だけで割り切れな
いのが人情であり、人間関係だ。
lines.english: He knew that rationally. But feelings and relationships refused to come out even, the way numbers did.

lines.japanese:
そして計算づくの交友を真理と知りつつ、割りき
れないのが忍だった。
lines.english: And Shinobu, though he knew every friendship was a calculation at heart, could never make the numbers settle.

lines.japanese:
勝手に室内に入ってみてはどうか？
　何度そう思ったことか。
lines.english: What if he simply let himself into the house? How many times had the thought occurred to him?

lines.japanese:
誘惑に駆られそうになる度に、垣というただそれ
だけのものでありながら、ある種結界にも似た強制
力に押し戻される。
lines.english: Each time temptation threatened to carry him away, the mere fence—nothing more than a fence—pushed him back with the force of some enchanted barrier.

lines.japanese:
踏み越えることには、絶大なエネルギーが必要だ。
　だが一度越えてしまえば、あとはさほど必要とは
しないものだ。
lines.english: Crossing it would take tremendous energy. Yet once he did, very little would be required after that.

lines.japanese: 一度越えれば、あとはずるずると行ってしまう。
lines.english: Once he crossed it, he would simply slide the rest of the way.

lines.japanese:
世に訓戒として語られるものに、その鉄則は多く
適用されている。
lines.english: That iron law applied to many of the world's cautionary maxims.

lines.japanese:
麻薬然り、借金然り。
　そのような理由で、忍は今だ笛子との邂逅を果た
せていない。
lines.english: Drugs, for instance. Debt, too. And for that very reason, Shinobu had yet to bring himself face-to-face with Fueko.

lines.japanese:
やがて……停滞している無意味さを悟ったのか、
忍は伊月家を離れた。
lines.english: Eventually... perhaps realizing there was no point in standing there any longer, Shinobu left the Izuki residence.

lines.japanese:
また数日後、忍は伊月家を訪れた。
　変化はない。
lines.english: Several days later, Shinobu visited the Izuki residence again. Nothing had changed.

lines.japanese:
閉めきった家は息を殺したようによそよそしい存
在であり、眼前に立つ忍をその素知らぬ様子でもっ
て拒絶していた。
lines.english: Sealed tight and holding its breath, the house stood aloof, rejecting Shinobu where he stood with an air of studied indifference.

lines.japanese:
それほど古い邸宅ではないはずだが、見れば壁は
所々がくすんでいる。
lines.english: It should not have been a particularly old house, yet patches of the walls looked dingy when he examined them.

lines.japanese:
流し見ればさほどでもない庭の荒れ具合も、こう
して凝視するとたちまち目立つものとなる。
lines.english: At a passing glance, the garden hardly seemed neglected. Under a steady gaze, though, the signs stood out at once.

lines.japanese:
誰も手入れをしていないのだ。きっと。
　庭の一角に植えられた木々が、小さく鳴った気が
した。
lines.english: Surely no one had been tending it. The trees planted in one corner of the garden seemed to rustle softly.

lines.japanese: 見ると木の隙間に少女の影が挟まっている。
lines.english: Looking closer, he saw the silhouette of a girl between the trees.

lines.japanese: 「……ねえ、笛子はいる？」
lines.english: “...Hey. Is Fueko home?”

lines.japanese:
声をかけると同時に、影はさっと向こう側に走り
去ってしまった。
lines.english: The moment he called to her, the shadow darted away to the far side.

lines.japanese:
笛子の妹だろう。
　しかし忍は、何度も会ったはずの少女の顔が、ど
うしても思い出せないのである。
lines.english: It must have been Fueko's little sister. And yet, try as he might, Shinobu could not remember the face of a girl he was sure he had met many times.

lines.japanese:
どうしても、などということがあるものか。
　改めて記憶をすくってみる。
lines.english: Try as he might? That was absurd. He sifted through his memory again.

lines.japanese:
喚起してみれば、確かにそれは思い出に残された
顔であった。
lines.english: When he called it to mind, the face was indeed there in his memories.

lines.japanese:
あの少女はどう生計を立てているのかと思われた。
　笛子が人目を忍んで買い物に出ているのか、ある
いは店屋物か。
lines.english: How was that girl getting by? Was Fueko slipping out unseen to shop, or were they having food delivered?

lines.japanese:
自宅にある食料を食いつないでいるのかも知れな
かった。
lines.english: Perhaps they were subsisting on whatever food remained in the house.

lines.japanese: 結局、今日もベルは押せない―――
lines.english: In the end, he could not ring the bell today either—

lines.japanese: 「ヘイ、忍くん」
lines.english: “Hey, Shinobu.”

lines.japanese: うじうじ悩んでいると、あずさに抱きつかれた。
lines.english: As he stood brooding, Azusa threw her arms around him.

lines.japanese: かすかな胸の感触が背中に感じられた。
lines.english: He felt the faint pressure of her chest against his back.

lines.japanese: ひとしきりじゃれついてから、ようやく身を離す。
lines.english: After teasing him for a while, she finally let go.

lines.japanese: 「捜しましたですよ」
lines.english: “I went looking for you, I did.”

lines.japanese: 線目で言う。
lines.english: Her eyes narrowed to lines as she spoke.
“...I see.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃ、行こうか」
lines.english: “Well, let's go.”

lines.japanese: 目的地も告げずに、あずさは忍の手を引いた。
lines.english: Azusa took Shinobu's hand and pulled him along without saying where.

lines.japanese: 「静かないい日だね」
lines.english: “It's a nice, quiet day.”
“...Is it?”

lines.japanese: 「こんなに、寂しいのに」
lines.english: “When it feels this lonely?”

lines.japanese: 「本当にそう思うの？」
lines.english: “Do you really think so?”

lines.japanese: 「この家々を見てごらんよ」
lines.english: “Look at all these houses.”

lines.japanese:
「人気のない昼間の住宅街は、墓場みたいな気が
　する」
lines.english: “A deserted neighborhood in the middle of the day feels like a graveyard.”

lines.japanese:
「この家のひとつひとつが、僕らにとっての工場み
　たいなものじゃないか」
lines.english: “Isn't every one of these houses something like what the factory is to us?”

lines.japanese: 「樋口章二が聖域と呼んだ場所」
lines.english: “A place Shouji Higuchi called a sanctuary.”

lines.japanese: 「ひとつひとつの聖域」
lines.english: “Each one, its own sanctuary.”

lines.japanese: 「だけど外側に立った人間から見ると」
lines.english: “But when you stand outside and look in—”

lines.japanese: 「……聖域は、悲しい」
lines.english: “...A sanctuary is a sad thing.”

lines.japanese: 「当人たちにとっては無上の価値であっても」
lines.english: “Even if it is supremely precious to the people inside.”

lines.japanese: 「いったん外に出ると、寂しいんだ」
lines.english: “Once you step outside, it's lonely.”

lines.japanese: 「僕らは失った」
lines.english: “We lost it.”

lines.japanese: 「細切れになってそれぞれの家に戻って」
lines.english: “We broke into pieces and went back to our separate houses.”

lines.japanese: 「……そして、無意味になる」
lines.english: “...And then we become meaningless.”

lines.japanese: 「別の意味になってしまうから」
lines.english: “Because it all takes on some other meaning.”

lines.japanese: 「何のために集ったのか、何のために深めたのか」
lines.english: “Why we came together, why we grew closer—”

lines.japanese: 「わからなくなる―――」
lines.english: “We lose sight of it—”

lines.japanese:
あずさは無言で聞いていた。
　ただ無力にそうしていたのではない。
　口を差し挟むタイミングを、辛抱強く待っていた。
lines.english: Azusa listened in silence. Not because she was helpless to do anything else. She patiently waited for a moment to speak.

lines.japanese: 待つだけではなく、忍が語る意味を噛みしめながら。
lines.english: And as she waited, she turned the meaning of Shinobu's words over in her mind.

lines.japanese: 「今日は静かないい日」
lines.english: “Today is a nice, quiet day.”

lines.japanese: 「あたしはそう思うよ」
lines.english: “That's what I think.”

lines.japanese: 「最近はね、そう思うんだよ」
lines.english: “Lately, that's what I've come to think.”

lines.japanese:
振り向きもしないあずさの表情が、どのようなも
のか忍にはわからない。
lines.english: Azusa did not turn around, so Shinobu could not tell what expression she wore.

lines.japanese:
と思っていると、こちらに向けられた顔が情けな
く苦笑する。
lines.english: Just as he thought that, she turned toward him with a helpless, wry smile.

lines.japanese:
「ま、ほら。あんなトラブルばっかりじゃ、身がも
　たないからさー。いかんべー。あれは。こわいし。
　きついし」
lines.english: “I mean, come on. If we had nothing but trouble like that, we'd never last. No way. It was scary. And rough.”

lines.japanese:
「いっくら美少女でも、できないことだってあるん
　だねぇ」
lines.english: “Guess there are things even a gorgeous girl can't do.”

lines.japanese: 「あはは……」
lines.english: “Ahaha...”

lines.japanese: 苦笑いを返すしかない。
lines.english: All he could do was return her strained smile.

lines.japanese: 「そんでもね」
lines.english: “But still—”

lines.japanese: 「あたしたちはここにいて、忍もいて」
lines.english: “We're all here. And you're here.”

lines.japanese: 「０じゃないから」
lines.english: “Because it isn't zero.”

lines.japanese: 「何もないわけじゃないから」
lines.english: “Because it's not as if we have nothing.”

lines.japanese: 「だから、我慢できるんじゃないかなぁ」
lines.english: “So I think we can bear it.”

lines.japanese:
「こないだすっごいこと考えたのさ。
　ちょうすごいこと」
lines.english: “I had this incredible thought the other day. Like, an absolutely incredible thought.”

lines.japanese: 「なに？」
lines.english: “What was it?”

lines.japanese: 「聞きたい？」
lines.english: “Want to hear?”

lines.japanese: 「うん」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese:
「うちらが生きて、生き続けて……
　そんでそのときまで仲良しでいられて」
lines.english: “Suppose we live and keep on living... and we're still all friends when the time comes.”

lines.japanese: 幸せな夢想だ、それは。
lines.english: It was a happy dream.

lines.japanese: 「……で、一人ずつ死んでいく」
lines.english: “...Then one by one, we die.”

lines.japanese: 避けられない事実だ、それは。
lines.english: It was an inescapable fact.

lines.japanese:
「あたしはその中で、何番目に死ぬんだろうなって
　思って」
lines.english: “And I started wondering where I'd come in that order.”

lines.japanese: 「最初は恐かった。死にたくないって思った」
lines.english: “It scared me at first. I thought, I don't want to die.”

lines.japanese:
「でもずーっと考えてると、あまりにも回避不能で
　……諦めるしかなかった」
lines.english: “But I kept thinking about it, and there was just no way to avoid it ...so I had to give in.”

lines.japanese: 「これが自然ってことなんだよね」
lines.english: “That's what it means for something to be natural, right?”

lines.japanese:
「受け入れられないくらい恐いけど、仕方ないって
　いうことで」
lines.english: “It's too scary to accept, but you don't get a choice in the matter.”

lines.japanese: 「そういう、もうどうしようもないパワーで」
lines.english: “That kind of force you just can't do anything about.”

lines.japanese:
「……だから死ぬときは、みんなすごく恐いはずな
　んだよね」
lines.english: “...So dying must be terribly scary for everyone, right?”

lines.japanese: 「そばに誰かに、いてほしいんだよね」
lines.english: “You'd want someone there beside you.”

lines.japanese:
「結婚して夫婦でいても、どっちかは先に死んで、
　どっちかがひとりぼっちで死ぬ」
lines.english: “Even if two people marry and stay together, one of them dies first, and the other dies all alone.”

lines.japanese:
「子供とかはいるかも知れないけど……
　いないかも知れないもんね」
lines.english: “They might have children... but then again, they might not.”

lines.japanese: 「で、あたしたちの場合ね」
lines.english: “But with us—”

lines.japanese: 「みんな結婚しないって言ってるの」
lines.english: “Everyone says they aren't going to get married.”

lines.japanese:
「結婚しないなら、ずっと遊んでいようって言った
　ら、いいよって」
lines.english: “So I said if none of us were getting married, we should keep having fun together forever, and they said yes.”

lines.japanese: 「葉子さんや沙也加ちゃんは、いいよって」
lines.english: “Youko and Sayaka both said yes.”

lines.japanese: 「忍くんとかも一緒でさ」
lines.english: “And you'd be with us, Shinobu.”

lines.japanese: 「いつまでも一緒で」
lines.english: “We'd always be together.”

lines.japanese: 「でね」
lines.english: “And then...”

lines.japanese:
一瞬だけ声がこわばった。
　急激で短い変化は、ある種の諦めと怯えを同居さ
せていた。
lines.english: For just an instant, her voice tightened. The sudden, fleeting change held both resignation and fear.

lines.japanese: 「一人ずつ、死んでいくんだ」
lines.english: “One by one, we'd die.”

lines.japanese:
気圧された忍がその足を重くすると、あずさは罪
のない笑みを作った。
lines.english: Shinobu slowed, overwhelmed, and Azusa put on an innocent smile.

lines.japanese: 「そんでね！」
lines.english: “And so!”

lines.japanese: しかしそれも一瞬のことだ。
lines.english: But that, too, lasted only an instant.

lines.japanese: 「あたしは、いつ死ぬのかなって思った」
lines.english: “I wondered when I'd die.”

lines.japanese: 「……いつ死ぬか？」
lines.english: “...When you might die?”

lines.japanese:
「あたしは一番若いけど、こんくらいの年の差じゃ
　寿命に差ができるかどうかはわからない」
lines.english: “I'm the youngest, but with an age gap this small, there's no telling whether it'll make any difference to our lifespans.”

lines.japanese:
「一番早いかも知れない。一番最後かも知れない。
　途中で事故や病気で死んじゃうかも知れない」
lines.english: “I might be first. I might be last. I might die in an accident or from an illness along the way.”

lines.japanese: 「死ぬのは恐い」
lines.english: “Dying is scary.”

lines.japanese: 「だけど……最期まで残るのも恐いよね」
lines.english: “But... being the last one left is scary, too.”
“...Yeah.”

lines.japanese:
自分にあてはめて考える。
　皆が死に絶え、自分ひとり。
lines.english: He tried to imagine it for himself. Everyone dead and gone. Himself alone.

lines.japanese:
特に忍のように他に心を許さない人間にとっては、
死の絶望と等価である。
lines.english: Especially for a person like Shinobu, who opened his heart to no one else, it was a despair equal to death itself.

lines.japanese: 「たぶんね、一番楽なのは……最初に逝くこと」
lines.english: “I think the easiest thing... would be to go first.”

lines.japanese: 「自分の死だけを我慢すればいいから」
lines.english: “Because then you only have to endure your own death.”

lines.japanese: 「次に楽なのは、二番目に死ぬこと」
lines.english: “The next easiest would be dying second.”

lines.japanese:

lines.japanese: 「みんなが生きた事実は残るって言うけど」

lines.english: He seized Azusa's head in one hand and squeezed.

lines.japanese: 「ぎー！　ぐー！」
lines.english: “Gyee! Guh!”

lines.japanese:
「……いや、その噂だけどよ。
　結構、信憑性がある話なんだよ」
lines.english: “...But about that rumor. It’s actually pretty credible.”

lines.japanese: 「この街が出所らしいじゃない」
lines.english: “Supposedly it started in this town.”

lines.japanese:
「辿るとな、もともとは他から伝搬してきた噂らし
　い」
lines.english: “Trace it back, and apparently the rumor was brought here from somewhere else.”

lines.japanese:
「普通、都市伝説ってやつは被害者の存在は明確じ
　ゃないんだが、こいつは違う」
lines.english: “Usually, an urban legend doesn't have any identifiable victims. This one's different.”

lines.japanese: 「実際に何人か消えてるんだ」
lines.english: “Several people have actually disappeared.”
“...Disappeared?”

lines.japanese: 「行方不明ってやつだな。失踪扱いだ」
lines.english: “Missing persons. Officially, they're just disappearances.”

lines.japanese:
「だから基本的には警察も動かない。まず家出の線
　を疑う。それで大きなニュースにはなっていない
　んだが」
lines.english: “Which means the police generally don't act. Their first suspicion is that somebody ran away. That's why it hasn't made major news, but...”

lines.japanese:
「その、他で発生してここで噂になってるのはさ、
　何か意味があるの？」
lines.english: “Does it mean anything that it began somewhere else but became a rumor here?”

lines.japanese: 「……これは、秘密の話なんだがな」
lines.english: “...This is confidential, though.”

lines.japanese: 興信所に知り合いのいる章二は、声を潜めた。
lines.english: Shouji, who had a contact at a private detective agency, lowered his voice.

lines.japanese:
だとしても芯の太い声はよく通るのだが、気分の
問題だろう。
lines.english: His deep, resonant voice still carried well, though; lowering it was probably more a matter of feeling.

lines.japanese: 「変質者だって言われてる」
lines.english: “They say it's some kind of deviant.”

lines.japanese: 「……多いよね」
lines.english: “...We sure have plenty of those.”

lines.japanese:
「そいつが犯行を繰り返しながら、潜伏場所を変え
　ながら移動してきた……という話があってな」
lines.english: “The story goes that this person has been moving from place to place, changing hideouts while committing one crime after another.”

lines.japanese: 「警察が事件性を認めているの？」
lines.english: “Do the police believe there are crimes involved?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、そうではないようだ」
lines.english: “No. Apparently not.”

lines.japanese:
「あくまでそういうヤツが放浪しているって話に過
　ぎないしな」
lines.english: “It's only a story about a person like that wandering around.”

lines.japanese: 「問題は、これも明らかな報告がないってことだ」
lines.english: “The problem is, there aren't any definite reports of this either.”

lines.japanese:
「そういう人物を見た、という風聞はあるんだが、
　じゃあどいつが見たのかいつ見たのかとなるとさ
　っぱりでな」
lines.english: “You hear rumors that somebody saw the person, but ask who saw them or when, and you get nothing.”

lines.japanese: 「本当に噂なんですね」
lines.english: “So it truly is nothing but a rumor.”

lines.japanese: 「それってただのホームレスなんじゃないの？」
lines.english: “Couldn't it just be a homeless person?”

lines.japanese: 「僕もそう思った」
lines.english: “I thought the same thing.”

lines.japanese: 「……さっきの失踪の話がここで出てくるんだが」
lines.english: “...This is where those disappearances come back into the story.”

lines.japanese:
「変質者の噂があるところと、若年層の連続失踪が
　地域的にも時間的にも同期してる」
lines.english: “Rumors of the deviant and the string of missing young people line up in both time and place.”

lines.japanese: 「……うーん。偶然じゃないわけだよね？」
lines.english: “...Hmm. So it isn't a coincidence, is it?”

lines.japanese:
「うちの事務所ではそう見てる。実際、捜索の依頼
　が来たんだ。その絡みもあって、牝豹所長殿はす
　ぐに警察とのパイプを使ったわけだ」
lines.english: “That's how everyone at our office sees it. We actually got a request to look for one of them. That was part of why Madam Panther immediately used her connections with the police.”

lines.japanese:
「するとな、不思議なくらい警察の方で無視されて
　いる、ということがわかった」
lines.english: “And that was when we discovered the police were ignoring it to an almost inexplicable degree.”

lines.japanese:
「現場レベルではいろいろな声があるようなんだが、
　どうもな……横やりが入っているって感じらしい」
lines.english: “There are all kinds of opinions on the ground, but... the general feeling is that somebody's sticking a spear in from the sidelines.”

lines.japanese: 「サイドジャベリン……」
lines.english: “A sideline javelin...”

lines.japanese: 「そうだ」
lines.english: “Right.”

lines.japanese: 「……つまらない男」
lines.english: “...What a dull man.”

lines.japanese: 「おい！」
lines.english: “Hey!”

lines.japanese:
「ではここで注目すべき議題として提案するのは最
　近になって私に新たに装備されるようになった体
　毛であるところの―――」
lines.english: “Then, as a matter worthy of our attention, I propose we discuss the body hair with which I have recently found myself newly equipped—”

lines.japanese: 「葉子、ほら知恵の輪」
lines.english: “Youko. Here—a wire puzzle.”

lines.japanese:
少女は短く叫んで、知的格闘を開始した。
　これは常人が挑めば解くのに十年かかると言われ
る代物であった。
lines.english: The girl gave a little cry and began her battle of wits. The puzzle was said to take an ordinary person ten years to solve.

lines.japanese: 「続けて」
lines.english: “Go on.”

lines.japanese:
「あ、ああ……要するに、警察に圧力をかけている
　何かがあって、その件について静観を命じている
　わけだ」
lines.english: “R-right... In short, somebody is pressuring the police and ordering them to stand by and leave the matter alone.”

lines.japanese:
「すでに少なくとも四人が失踪してる。家出なんざ
　日常的に起こるだろうがな、これは明らかにおか
　しい数と時期だ」
lines.english: “At least four people have already disappeared. Runaways happen every day, sure, but these numbers and this timing are clearly wrong.”

lines.japanese:
「……警察に誰が何の目的でそうした圧力をかけて
　いるのかわからない。ただ、内部的にはちょっと
　した禁忌という話らしいな」
lines.english: “...I don’t know who’s putting that pressure on the police or why. But apparently, inside the department, the whole subject is a bit of a taboo.”

lines.japanese: 「つまり失踪者は犠牲者……ということ？」
lines.english: “So the missing people are victims... Is that what you mean?”

lines.japanese: 「そうだろうな」
lines.english: “Probably.”

lines.japanese: さらりと章二は認めた。
lines.english: Shouji said it as though it were nothing.

lines.japanese: 「殺されてる。変態のすることだしな」
lines.english: “They're being killed. It's the work of some pervert.”

lines.japanese: 「サイコパス、か」
lines.english: “A psychopath, you mean?”

lines.japanese: 「サイコパワー？」
lines.english: “Psychic powers?”

lines.japanese:
「頭がおかしくなって、わけのわからない理由で人
　を殺す人のことだよ」
lines.english: “Someone who loses their mind and kills people for reasons nobody can understand.”

lines.japanese: 「……え？　その四人って殺されたの？」
lines.english: “...Wait. You mean those four people were killed?”

lines.japanese:
「決まったわけじゃないが、全部が家出だとは考え
　られん」
lines.english: “Nothing's been proven, but I can't believe every one of them ran away.”

lines.japanese:
「ま、十中八九やられてる。しかも、死体が見つから
　ず犯行も目撃されない」
lines.english: “Odds are they've been killed. And yet no bodies have turned up, and nobody witnessed a crime.”

lines.japanese:
「ただ徘徊する怪人の存在感だけが漂って、そして
　実際に人が減っているだけだ」
lines.english: “All we have is the presence of some strange figure roaming around, and the fact that people are disappearing.”

lines.japanese:
「……なあ、数人もの人間を街中で誰の目にも止ま
　らず処置して、腐る骸を発見されもせずに隠し通
　せるものか？」
lines.english: “...Tell me: could someone dispose of several people in town without a soul noticing, then keep their rotting remains hidden and undiscovered?”

lines.japanese: 「人目につかない場所……」
lines.english: “Somewhere out of sight...”

lines.japanese: 「森とか？」
lines.english: “The woods, perhaps?”

lines.japanese: 「……まあ、それも一つだな」
lines.english: “...Well, that's one possibility.”

lines.japanese: 「近いで！？」
lines.english: “That's right next door!”

lines.japanese: 「あとは……廃工場群」
lines.english: “Or... the abandoned factories.”
“Whoa?!”

lines.japanese: 「……調べておいたぜ。何もなかった」
lines.english: “...I checked. There was nothing there.”

lines.japanese: 「仕事が速い」
lines.english: “Fast work.”

lines.japanese: 「ククク、もっと誉めていいぜ」
lines.english: “Heh-heh-heh. You can praise me more than that.”

lines.japanese: 「……ただな、一つ気になる話がある」
lines.english: “...There is one other thing bothering me, though.”

lines.japanese: 「気になる話だらけじゃないの。で、今度は？」
lines.english: “Everything you’ve told us is worrying. What’s this one?”

lines.japanese: 斎が読んでいた新聞を忍に渡した。
lines.english: Itsuki handed Shinobu the newspaper he had been reading.

lines.japanese: 「原因不明の死者……」
lines.english: “Unexplained deaths...”

lines.japanese:
「……女子校生ばかりを狙った……犠牲者２名、
　重症１名……」
lines.english: “...Schoolgirls targeted... two dead, one seriously injured...”

lines.japanese:
「ニュースでやっていたわね。
　それと関連があるということ？」
lines.english: “That was on the news. You think it's connected?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese:
「失踪した犠牲者と、この路上で殺害された女子高
　生と……その差は何なのかしら？」
lines.english: “What distinguishes the missing victims from the schoolgirls killed in the street, I wonder?”

lines.japanese: 「単純な理由だろうな」
lines.english: “Probably something simple.”

lines.japanese: 「目につかないところで殺されて、そのままなんだ」
lines.english: “They were killed somewhere out of sight and simply left there.”

lines.japanese:
「意外と、その森あたりに死体が埋まっているかも
　知れないぜ？」
lines.english: “You know, there might be bodies buried in those woods after all.”

lines.japanese:
「まあそれもあって工場を調べてたんだが……
　特に何もなかった。安心するがいい」
lines.english: “That was one reason I searched the factory... but there was nothing there. You can rest easy.”

lines.japanese: 「本当に安心できるよ、それは」
lines.english: “Now that really is a relief.”

lines.japanese:
「うちの所長様はな、意外と街中じゃないかって予
　想してる」
lines.english: “Our illustrious chief actually suspects it may be somewhere in the middle of town.”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese:
「デッドスペースだよ。都会にだってある。いや……
　人がいればいるほど死角が生まれるのが街だ。森や
　廃墟に死体を隠すなんざ、誰だって考えるさ」
lines.english: “Dead space. Cities have it, too. No... the more people there are, the more blind spots a city creates. Anybody would think of hiding bodies in the woods or in ruins.”

lines.japanese:
「……正直、あっちの森向こうの工場街な、警察が
　調べたみたいだぞ。今はそういった捜査活動も厳
　重に禁じられているがな」
lines.english: “...To be honest, the police apparently searched the factory district on the far side of those woods. That sort of investigation has since been strictly forbidden, though.”

lines.japanese: 「ここは安全……か」
lines.english: “So this place is safe...”

lines.japanese: 「いろいろとメリットがあるわけだ」
lines.english: “Meaning this place has a few advantages.”

lines.japanese: 「ちなみに凶器なんだが……不明らしい」
lines.english: “As for the weapon... apparently they don't know.”

lines.japanese:
「刃物の類か、銃器か、毒物か……
　いろいろあるとは思うけど、不明？」
lines.english: “A blade, a firearm, poison... There are plenty of possibilities, but they don't know?”

lines.japanese: 「外傷なんだがな、これが少しおかしい」
lines.english: “There was an external wound, but something about it was wrong.”

lines.japanese:
「死因は頭部の傷ということにはなっちゃいるんだ
　が……普通の傷じゃないようだ」
lines.english: “They've put the official cause of death down as a head wound... but apparently it was no ordinary injury.”
“...Then what was it?”

lines.japanese: 「槍か？」
lines.english: “A spear?”

lines.japanese: 「アメちゃんやるから黙ってろ、な？」
lines.english: “I'll give you some candy if you'll keep quiet, okay?”

lines.japanese: 「むぎー！」
lines.english: “Mrrgh!”

lines.japanese: あずさはアメちゃんを口に放り込んで噛み砕いた。
lines.english: Azusa popped the candy into her mouth and crunched it.

lines.japanese:
「ここからはソースが別になるんで確定じゃないん
　だが……まず傷に異物の痕跡はなかったそうだ」
lines.english: “This next part comes from a different source, so it isn’t confirmed... First, they apparently found no trace of foreign material in the wound.”

lines.japanese: 「……飛び道具じゃないってことか」
lines.english: “...Meaning it wasn't a projectile.”

lines.japanese:
「一般的に売っている工具・刃物の類でもない。
　あれはけっこう特定される」
lines.english: “It wasn't any commercially available tool or blade either. Those are fairly easy to identify.”

lines.japanese:
「確かに槍状のもので突けば、事後も残るものでは
　ないけれど」
lines.english: “True. If they were stabbed with something spear-shaped, the weapon itself would not remain afterward.”

lines.japanese:
「傷痕から凶器の特定ができる。
　が、今回はそれがわからない」
lines.english: “But the wound normally identifies the weapon. This time, it didn't.”

lines.japanese: 「どういう傷なの？」
lines.english: “What kind of wound was it?”

lines.japanese: 「なんでも」
lines.english: “Supposedly...”

lines.japanese:
「頭蓋と皮膚が溶けて、棒を差し込まれたような脳
　の損傷が」
lines.english: “The skin and skull had melted, and the brain was damaged as though someone had thrust a rod inside.”

lines.japanese: 「それって槍じゃん……」
lines.english: “That sounds like a spear...”

lines.japanese: 「長い棒を槍と言うならそうだ」
lines.english: “If you call any long stick a spear, then sure.”

lines.japanese: 「棒の種類がわからないの？」
lines.english: “They couldn't identify what kind of rod it was?”

lines.japanese: 「そこらの木の枝とか」
lines.english: “What about a branch off some tree?”

lines.japanese: 「それなら簡単にわかるぜ」
lines.english: “They'd identify that easily.”

lines.japanese:
「……まあ、さらに眉唾な話が続く。
　この穴と脳の損傷だが、ずれてる」
lines.english: “...Well, what comes next is even harder to swallow. The hole and the damage to the brain don't line up.”

lines.japanese: 「ずれてる……」
lines.english: “They don't line up...?”

lines.japanese:
「棒を突っ込んで頭蓋が陥没した。これはいい。
　その下の脳が損傷した。これもいい」
lines.english: “A rod was driven in, caving in the skull. Fine. The brain beneath it was damaged. Fine.”

lines.japanese:
「……頭蓋の穴と脳の損傷に、ズレがある。まるで
　穴を開けてから、脳だけをぐるりとずらしたかの
　ように」
lines.english: “...But the hole in the skull and the damage to the brain are offset. As though somebody opened the hole and then rotated the brain beneath it.”

lines.japanese: 「イタイイタイタイイタイ……」
lines.english: “Ow ow ow ow ow...”

lines.japanese: あずさが自分を抱くようにして身をくねらせた。
lines.english: Azusa hugged herself and writhed.

lines.japanese: 「まるで」
lines.english: “It's almost as if...”

lines.japanese: 「体が負傷を勘違いしたみたいだね」
lines.english: “It's as if the body got its own injury wrong.”

lines.japanese: 「……オレの情報はここまでだ」
lines.english: “...That's all the information I have.”

lines.japanese: 「本当に殺人事件なのかしらね、それ」
lines.english: “I wonder if it was even murder.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん……」

「直接の死因は頭部の傷じゃなく、ショック死って
　話もあってな……まあ傷が引き金なんだろうが……
　いまいち要領を得ない話さ」
lines.english: “I've also heard the immediate cause wasn't the head wound but shock... Though the wound probably triggered it... None of it is very clear.”

lines.japanese:
「隔たる傷、発見されない死体、曖昧な死因、姿の
　ない怪人」
lines.english: “A displaced wound. Bodies never found. An uncertain cause of death. A figure no one sees.”

lines.japanese: 「……目撃例がないのに噂だけ流れるってのもな」
lines.english: “...And rumors spreading without a single eyewitness.”

lines.japanese: 「そういうものよ」
lines.english: “That is how it works.”

lines.japanese: 「……なんだと？」
lines.english: “...What did you say?”

lines.japanese: 「偏向するということは、変質するということ」
lines.english: “Deviation means transformation.”

lines.japanese: 「人でありながら、異なる者になること」
lines.english: “To remain human, yet become other.”

lines.japanese:
「私たちはそうした存在を見ても、人とは思わない
　ことを選択する」
lines.english: “When we look upon such beings, we choose not to regard them as human.”

lines.japanese: 「だから目に入っても見なかったことにしてしまう」
lines.english: “And so even when they enter our field of vision, we pretend we never saw them.”

lines.japanese: 「……そんなことがあるか。目に入ったら、わかる」
lines.english: “...That's ridiculous. If something enters your vision, you see it.”

lines.japanese:
「ずれた心によって獲得する形質が、もし空気のそ
　れと酷似していたら？」
lines.english: “What if the traits a distorted mind gave someone closely resembled the qualities of air?”

lines.japanese: 「あん？」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese:
「大気の持つ性質を私たちは知っている。そしてそ
　れが目に入らないものと理解している」
lines.english: “We know the properties of air. And we understand that air is invisible to us.”

lines.japanese:
「狂った心がその宿主に空気的な性質を与えた時……
　私たちはその人物から受ける情報を異化することが
　できなくなる」
lines.english: “When a deranged mind gives its host the properties of air... we can no longer register the information we receive from that person as something distinct.”

lines.japanese: 「……理解できなくなる」
lines.english: “...We become incapable of understanding it.”

lines.japanese:
「つまり外見は変わらずとも、中身が変わったら透
　明人間になるってことか？」
lines.english: “You're saying someone becomes invisible when the inside changes, even if their appearance stays the same?”

lines.japanese: 「そうなることもあるかも、という話」
lines.english: “I'm only saying that it might happen.”

lines.japanese: 「ナンセンスだな」
lines.english: “Nonsense.”

lines.japanese:
「むしろ怪しい部分が強調されれば、目に付くって
　考える方が普通だ。心構え一つで目に入らなくな
　るなんて……」
lines.english: “Normally, you'd expect the suspicious parts to stand out and attract attention. Yet you're saying someone can vanish from sight through nothing but a state of mind...?”

lines.japanese: 「ありますよ」
lines.english: “Such things exist.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「そういう技術、ありますよ」
lines.english: “There are techniques like that.”

lines.japanese: 知恵の輪に熱中しながら、顔も上げずに言う。
lines.english: She spoke without looking up, engrossed in the wire puzzle.

lines.japanese:
「ちょっと違いますけど、要するに盲点を突くって
　感じで……視野に立っているのに存在を感じさせ
　ないよう気配を殺したり、」
lines.english: “It is somewhat different, but the basic idea is to exploit a blind spot... to stand within a person's field of view while suppressing your presence so completely that they do not sense you, or—”

lines.japanese:
「あと複数人の視野を計算してその死角に身を滑らせ
　ることで、群衆の中にありながら群衆の目から身を
　隠す……というぶじゅつのおーぎが」
lines.english: “To calculate the visual fields of several people and slip into their blind spots, thereby hiding from the eyes of a crowd while moving among it... There is a secret martial-arts technique where—”

lines.japanese: 「夢枕漠然とした設定だなそいつは」
lines.english: “A premise vague enough for a Baku Yumemakura novel.”

lines.japanese: 「設定言われた……」
lines.english: “He called it a premise...”

lines.japanese: 「気配を消すというのはわかるとしてもだな」
lines.english: “I can at least understand concealing your presence, but...”

lines.japanese:
「気配を消すというは、一種の変質のことよ。
　音を消すだけが全てではないわ」
lines.english: “Concealing one's presence is a form of alteration. It is not merely a question of suppressing sound.”

lines.japanese:
「にしてもおまえ。じゃどうして怪人の噂なんての
　が流れる？　透明なら噂にもならんはずだ」
lines.english: “Even so, explain why rumors about this figure spread at all. If the person were invisible, nobody would talk about them.”

lines.japanese: 「だから」
lines.english: “That's precisely why.”

lines.japanese: ごく当たり前のことであるかのように。
lines.english: As though it were the most obvious thing in the world.

lines.japanese: 「彼らは大概は目に入っているのよ、章二」
lines.english: “Most of the time, they do enter our field of vision, Shouji.”
“What...?”

lines.japanese:
「そこにいた気がする。いたような気がする。
　しかし思い出せない」
lines.english: “You feel they were there. You have the impression they were there. But you can’t remember.”

lines.japanese:
「我々が時に何度も会っているはずの親族の顔を思い
　出すことができないように、」
lines.english: “Like when we cannot recall the face of a relative we must have met many times—”

lines.japanese:
「いたはずなのにどうしても知覚記録を読み出せない
　存在、マスクされた存在」
lines.english: “Someone who must have been there, yet whose perceptual record we are utterly unable to retrieve. A masked existence.”

lines.japanese:
「彼らは平然と視野を横切り活動しているというの
　に、私たちはその実像に焦点を結ぶことができな
　い。焦点を外されれば情報は劣化するものよ」
lines.english: “They pass calmly across our field of view and go about their business, yet we cannot bring their true form into focus. Once focus slips, information deteriorates.”

lines.japanese:
「そして焦点というものは受信側の認識に左右され
　る。私たちが騙し絵をそうと知るまで認知できな
　いのと同様に」
lines.english: “And focus depends upon the receiver's recognition. Just as we cannot perceive an optical illusion for what it is until we recognize it.”

lines.japanese: 「だから噂になり得る」
lines.english: “That is what allows rumors of them to exist.”

lines.japanese:
「かすかに意識にひっかかるその異物を、時間をかけ
　たり正常認知と掛け合わせて比較したりすることで
　かろうじてその奇観を証拠映像として抽出できる」
lines.english: “Only by dwelling on the foreign presence that barely catches in our awareness, or comparing it over time against normal perception, can we manage to extract an image of that uncanny sight as evidence.”

lines.japanese: 「おぼろな影として―――」
lines.english: “As a hazy shadow—”

lines.japanese: 「……いや、だがな……普通は、」
lines.english: “...No, but... normally—”

lines.japanese: 「普通では有り得ない」
lines.english: “Normally, it would be impossible.”

lines.japanese:
「だから……彼らは猟奇殺人犯と呼ばれる。
　呼ばれたのよ」
lines.english: “That is why... they are called grotesque killers. That is how they came to be called that.”

lines.japanese:
「対象としての猟奇趣味ではなく、存在自体が異な
　った方角を向いている……相違を常として求める
　者としての猟奇ね」
lines.english: “The grotesque is not the object of their fascination. Their very existence faces in another direction... Their grotesquerie lies in their constant pursuit of difference.”

lines.japanese: 「……正確には、逸脱者とでも言うべき存在よ」
lines.english: “...More precisely, perhaps we should call them deviants.”

lines.japanese:
「最初は人であったはずの彼らがそうなるためには、
　大きな認知上の変化が必要」
lines.english: “For beings who must originally have been human to become like that, their cognition must undergo a profound change.”

lines.japanese:
「そして自らの身を隠し、形質変化による異常行動
　を支えるための……ある種の嗜好特化が」
lines.english: “And to conceal themselves and sustain the abnormal behavior arising from that change in their traits... a kind of specialization of preference.”

lines.japanese: 「姿が見えない異常者は、全てエリートなの」
lines.english: “Every unseen aberrant is an elite.”

lines.japanese: 「異質な者たちのね」
lines.english: “An elite among those who differ, I mean.”

lines.japanese:
「そいつらなら、見つからずに忍び寄って人を殺せ
　ると？」
lines.english: “So they could creep up unnoticed and kill someone?”

lines.japanese: 「できるでしょうね」
lines.english: “I imagine they could.”

lines.japanese:
「……そういった者たちは、人に注視されることを
　極度に恐れるものだから」
lines.english: “...People like that tend to have an extreme fear of being watched.”

lines.japanese:
「半生を部屋の中で過ごし、視線を避け、そのこと
　が本能として焼き付けられた段階での……発症」
lines.english: “Half a lifetime spent in a room, avoiding every gaze, until that avoidance has burned itself into instinct... and then, the onset.”

lines.japanese:
「もし認識の変化を獲得できたなら……世界そのも
　のが個室になる」
lines.english: “If they can acquire that change in recognition... the world itself becomes a private room.”

lines.japanese: 「こんな人が大勢いる個室があるかよ」
lines.english: “What kind of private room has this many people in it?”

lines.japanese: 「章二、あなたは個室で何をする？」
lines.english: “Shouji. What do you do in the privacy of your room?”

lines.japanese: 「人に言えないことは何もしない？」
lines.english: “You don't do anything you couldn't tell anyone else about?”

lines.japanese: 「してるつもりはない」
lines.english: “Not that I know of.”

lines.japanese:
「では、あなたが自室で女と交わるとするなら、そ
　れはどう？」
lines.english: “Then suppose you were to have intercourse with a woman in your room. What then?”

lines.japanese: 「バカ、何言ってる！」
lines.english: “Idiot! What are you talking about?!”

lines.japanese:
「その方法に、特殊なものがあったとしたら？
　例えば―――」
lines.english: “And what if you had some unusual way of doing it? For instance—”

lines.japanese: 「やめろ！　ここは―――」
lines.english: “Stop! This isn't the place—”

lines.japanese: 「ふぇ？　まじわり？」
lines.english: “Huh? Intercourse?”

lines.japanese: 章二が沙也加の胸ぐらを掴む。
lines.english: Shouji seized Sayaka by the collar.

lines.japanese: 「場所を考えろ！」
lines.english: “Think about where you are!”

lines.japanese: 「ちょっとちょっと、本気ケンカだめだよ！」
lines.english: “Hey, hey! No real fighting!”

lines.japanese:
噴出しかけた怒りを呑む努力を、忍は親友の苦悶
に見た。
lines.english: In his best friend's anguish, Shinobu saw the effort it took to swallow the anger threatening to burst out.

lines.japanese:
「……悪ぃ。おひぃさんに手出したら国家反逆罪も
　のだな」
lines.english: “...Sorry. Lay a hand on Her Highness and it's practically treason, huh?”

lines.japanese:
「あなたは……そうね、あなたにとって真の個室は
　……自宅ではなかったわね」
lines.english: “You... yes. For you, the truly private room wasn’t your own home.”

lines.japanese:
「ごめんなさい。
　このたとえはあなたには該当しない」
lines.english: “I'm sorry. That analogy doesn't apply to you.”

lines.japanese: 「……いいさ」
lines.english: “...It's all right.”

lines.japanese:
「つまりさ、個室となった世界で、趣味を爆発させ
　てしまうってことだね。彼らは」
lines.english: “So, once the world becomes their private room, they let their obsessions run wild. Is that it?”

lines.japanese: 「そういう心の動きだと思うわ」
lines.english: “I think that's the impulse at work.”

lines.japanese: 「世界の個室化……か」
lines.english: “A world turned into a private room...”

lines.japanese:
「そういう異常な心の動き、確かにあるのかも知れ
　ないな」
lines.english: “Maybe that kind of warped impulse really does exist.”

lines.japanese:
「……だけど……だとしたら、オレはそいつらを許
　さん」
lines.english: “...But if it does, I won't forgive them.”

lines.japanese: 「なぜ？」
lines.english: “Why?”

lines.japanese:
「今回のコイツは……
　オレらの学校からすでに一人を殺している」
lines.english: “This one... has already killed someone from our school.”

lines.japanese: 「……それは、新聞に載っているこの？」
lines.english: “...You mean this case in the paper?”

lines.japanese:
「そうだ。依頼人の娘だ。
　オレの学校ってんで、調べろとな」
lines.english: “Right. The client’s daughter. Since she went to my school, I was told to look into it.”

lines.japanese:
「失踪届はまだ出されていない。が、恐らくもう死
　んでいる。どこか、人の目の届かない場所で」
lines.english: “No missing-person report has been filed yet. But she's probably dead already, somewhere out of sight.”

lines.japanese: 「じき発見されるさ。死体は腐る」
lines.english: “They'll find her soon enough. Bodies rot.”

lines.japanese: 「……すぐ、近くなんだ……この事件って……」
lines.english: “...This case... is happening so close to us...”

lines.japanese:
「……ま、そのことはこっちの話なんで、おまえら
　は気にしないでいいけどな」
lines.english: “...Well, that part's on my end, so the rest of you don't need to worry about it.”

lines.japanese: 「正直、確かにおかしいとは思う」
lines.english: “Honestly, yeah, something about this does feel off.”

lines.japanese:
「死体があるのに死因さえもわからん。関連づけて
　考えることさえ禁じられている。誰が警察に圧力
　をかけているのか知らんが、意図もわからん」
lines.english: “There are bodies, but they can't even determine a cause of death. They're not even allowed to consider the cases connected. I don't know who's pressuring the police, or why.”

lines.japanese:
「もしこの事件全体を隠すためなら、失踪事件につ
　いても制限がかかるはずだしな」
lines.english: “If they were trying to bury the whole case, they'd be clamping down on the missing-person cases too.”

lines.japanese: 「……まさに意図を隠すためだと思うよ」
lines.english: “...That's exactly it. I think it's meant to conceal their intent.”

lines.japanese: 「なんの意図だ」
lines.english: “What purpose?”

lines.japanese: 「その二つが関連しているという、ね」
lines.english: “That the two are connected, I mean.”

lines.japanese:
「立て続けに介入すれば、当然そういうことを考え
　るヤツも出てくる」
lines.english: “If they kept interfering, of course people would start thinking exactly that.”

lines.japanese:
「自分たちで何とかするつもりなんじゃないかな。
　だから強引に圧力をかける」
lines.english: “Maybe they plan to deal with it themselves. That's why they're being so heavy-handed.”

lines.japanese: 「その偉い人が解決してくれればいいのだけれど」
lines.english: “I just hope the big shot behind it can solve everything.”

lines.japanese:
「他人事じゃない。
　もし回りでそういう事件が起こったら―――」
lines.english: “This concerns us, too. If something like that happened to someone around us—”

lines.japanese: 「……もし、おまえらが……」
lines.english: “...If one of you...”

lines.japanese:
言葉がまとまらなかったのか。
　章二は顔を手で覆い、低く呻いた。
　それを見る忍の顔に、深い翳りがさす。
lines.english: Perhaps words failed him. Shouji covered his face with one hand and gave a low groan. Watching him, a deep shadow crossed Shinobu's face.

lines.japanese: 「おまえも気がかりか？」
lines.english: “You're worried too?”

lines.japanese: 「……うん……心配だ」
lines.english: “...Yes... I am.”

lines.japanese:
「最近、いやもうずっと……
　こういう事件ばかりでさ」
lines.english: “These days—no, for a long time now... it's been one case like this after another.”

lines.japanese: 「だとしても……世の中のせいになんてしたかない」
lines.english: “Even so... I don't want to blame the world for it.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだね」
lines.english: “You're right.”

lines.japanese:
しかし章二は全ての可能性は検討していないな、
と忍は思った。
lines.english: But Shouji hadn't considered every possibility, Shinobu thought.

lines.japanese: その『もし』には、決定的な悲劇が欠けている。
lines.english: That ‘what if’ left out the decisive tragedy.

lines.japanese:
忍の気がかりとはまさにそれであり、口に出すわ
けにはいかない狂気の論理だった。
lines.english: And that was precisely what troubled Shinobu: the mad logic he could never voice.

lines.japanese:
即ち……身内からそうした者が出た場合。
　聖域の仲間を奪い、汚し、否定し……
　あるいは―――
lines.english: Namely... what if someone like that was one of them? What if they took one of their friends in the sanctuary, defiled them, denied them... Or else—

lines.japanese: 「ま……そうならないようにしてやるさ」
lines.english: “Well... I'll make sure it never comes to that.”

lines.japanese: 「ねえ、もし」
lines.english: “Hey... what if—”

lines.japanese: 「もし、そういう人間が……そばにあらわれたら？」
lines.english: “What if someone like that... showed up right beside us?”

lines.japanese: 「……決まってる」
lines.english: “...The answer's obvious.”

lines.japanese:
「いや、決めただろ。
　ヤバい時は、オレが前衛、おまえがケツ拭き」
lines.english: “No—we already decided. When things get bad, I'm the front line, and you clean up the mess.”

lines.japanese: 「それでうまくいくだろ」
lines.english: “That should work, right?”

lines.japanese: 「……そうだね」
lines.english: “...Right.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだろあずさ？」
lines.english: “Right, Azusa?”

lines.japanese: 会話について来られなかった少女を忍は見やる。
lines.english: Shinobu glanced at the girl, who had lost the thread of the conversation.

lines.japanese:
「あずさ、夜はひとりで出歩かないようにってこと
　だよ」
lines.english: “Azusa, the point is that you shouldn't go out alone at night.”

lines.japanese: 「おーう」
lines.english: “Okaaay.”

lines.japanese: 「いつもは門限あるし、平気だよ」
lines.english: “I've got a curfew anyway, so I'll be fine.”

lines.japanese: 「それだけで充分と思うか？」
lines.english: “You really think that's enough?”

lines.japanese: 「オレは、夕方こそ危険だと思うぜ」
lines.english: “I think dusk is when it's most dangerous.”

lines.japanese: 「なんで？」
lines.english: “Why?”

lines.japanese:
誰も答えない。
　同感だったからだ。
　葉子の場違いな声が、沈黙に異物として混入した。
lines.english: No one answered. They all felt the same. Youko's incongruous voice intruded on the silence like a foreign body.

lines.japanese: 「解けました、これ」
lines.english: “I solved it.”

lines.japanese: 心を乱した者たちについて―――
lines.english: On those whose minds have fallen into disorder—

lines.japanese:
その不可思議な人間たちが、いつ頃から存在していたのか……いくら歴史
を辿っても明確な回答は得られない。
lines.english: When did these uncanny people first appear? No matter how far back we trace history, no clear answer presents itself.

lines.japanese:
人類史には空白がいくつもあり、歴史とは事実上無数に分断された断片
を、検証と想像によって繋ぎあわせたものに過ぎない。
　古代から乱心はあったろうし、事実通常とは異なった精神状態を示す言葉
も数多く残る。
lines.english: Human history is riddled with blank spaces. In practice, history is nothing more than countless severed fragments joined together through verification and imagination. Madness likely existed in antiquity, and many words remain for states of mind outside the ordinary.

lines.japanese:
サイコパスやソシオパスなどの不適切な用語、そして反社会性人格障害な
どとも異なる。
lines.english: This is distinct from ill-chosen labels such as psychopath and sociopath, and also from antisocial personality disorder.

lines.japanese: まったく新しい形の異常者像。
lines.english: An entirely new conception of the aberrant.

lines.japanese: 心が変質するということ。
lines.english: A transformation of the mind.

lines.japanese:
いわゆる変異とは違い、内面の問題である。
　猿と人が明確に異なるようには、見て取れない。
lines.english: Unlike what we commonly call mutation, this is an inward matter. It cannot be discerned as plainly as the difference between an ape and a human being.

lines.japanese: 心的変化とは行動の変化である。
lines.english: A change in the mind is a change in behavior.

lines.japanese: 倫理の破壊である。
lines.english: It is the destruction of ethics.

lines.japanese:
周囲の個体と、概ね同じ倫理を持っている限り群れは成立するだろう。
　成立―――決闘や闘争による死や略奪もまた含まれる。自然なことだから
だ。
　社会がある以上、そういったことは起こりうるものだからだ。
lines.english: A pack can exist so long as its members share, by and large, the same ethics. Exist—even when duels and conflicts bring death or plunder. Those things are natural. Where there is society, such things can occur.

lines.japanese: しかし心の変質は違う。
lines.english: But mental transformation is different.

lines.japanese: それによって外れることは、違う。
lines.english: To fall outside the pack through such a change is another matter.

lines.japanese:
新しい論理は古い思考を侵略し上書きされる。
　時にそれは自らの恒常性さえ破壊することがある。
　死の確定であり、さほど重要な問題ではない。
lines.english: A new logic invades and overwrites the old mode of thought. At times, it may destroy even one's own homeostasis. That means certain death, but it is not an especially important problem.

lines.japanese:
強固な本能を保持できたとしよう。
　その場合、錯乱した個体は命を繋ぐことは可能だ。
lines.english: Suppose, however, that the individual retains powerful instincts. In that case, the deranged individual may survive.

lines.japanese:
しかし社会性を失った個体は、群れに留まることはできない。
　ルールを踏み越える者は、村八分にされるか打ち殺されることになる。
lines.english: But an individual that has lost its social nature cannot remain with the pack. Those who transgress its rules will be ostracized or beaten to death.

lines.japanese: 乱雑に論ずるなら、大半の異常者はそうだった。
lines.english: To put it crudely, this was true of most aberrant people.

lines.japanese: ごく希に、該当しない者がいた。
lines.english: Very rarely, someone proved an exception.

lines.japanese:
人の生活をなぞり、あるいは隠れ通しながら……彼らは人を逸することが
できた。
　いや、これもできたから生き残れたと言うべきか。
lines.english: By mimicking the contours of human life, or else remaining hidden throughout... they could pass beyond the bounds of humanity. Or rather, we should say they survived because they could do this.

lines.japanese: 社会からの監視を逃れる特異な力は、決して超能力の類などではない。
lines.english: This peculiar ability to escape society’s scrutiny is no psychic power.

lines.japanese:
単純には気配を断つ能力。
　散布される自らの存在感を隠蔽し、
　視線に対して鋭敏に対応できる精神状態を保ち、
　表層的社会性を保持する。
　この三つを兼ね備えた時、人体は限りなく透明になる。
lines.english: Put simply, it is the ability to extinguish one’s presence. To conceal the presence one gives off. To maintain a mental state keenly responsive to the gaze. To maintain the outward forms of social behavior. When all three coincide, the human body becomes all but transparent.

lines.japanese: 三項目で刮目すべきは、視線についてであろうか。
lines.english: Of the three, the gaze is perhaps most worthy of attention.

lines.japanese:
古来、目は力を持つとされた。
　邪な眼は呪いと同義であり、見られることは忌避された。
　雑学者と蔑まれた南方熊楠は、この概念を邪視と訳した。
lines.english: Since antiquity, the eye has been held to possess power. The evil eye was synonymous with a curse, and being watched was abhorred. Kumagusu Minakata—derided as a mere collector of trivia—rendered this concept in Japanese as jashi—‘evil eye.’

lines.japanese: 信仰領域に立ち入らずとも、視線の恐怖は本邦にも存在するものである。
lines.english: Even without venturing into the realm of faith, fear of the gaze exists in Japan too.

lines.japanese:
相違した者を焙る。
　外れた者を焦がす。
　精神を焼き尽くす、耐え難い苦痛。
lines.english: It sears those who are different. Scorches those who stray. An unbearable agony that burns the mind to ash.

lines.japanese:
社会性という長大なレールに乗っていれば浴びることも少ないそれは、し
かしふとしたはずみで誰にでも焦点を結ぶ、刹那的な代物だ。
lines.english: Those who remain on the long track of social conformity seldom suffer it. Yet some chance event can bring anyone into focus, if only for an instant.

lines.japanese:
異常性を自覚する者は、白日に晒されることを恐れる。視線を恐れる。
　彼らは擬態の術を身につける。
lines.english: Those conscious of their abnormality fear being dragged into broad daylight. They fear the gaze. They learn to camouflage themselves.

lines.japanese:
最も簡単なことは、部屋にこもることだ。
　誰と会わなければ外に出る必要もないのである。
lines.english: The simplest thing is to shut oneself away in a room. If one meets no one, one has no need to go outside.

lines.japanese:
ネットワークによって周辺情報を削除することで、疎隔感は低減できる。
　文字だけの存在であるなら、彼はどのような英雄的な存在にもなれる。
　往々にして、そうした存在はふとしたはずみで攻撃側に回りやすい。
lines.english: By using the network to erase the surrounding context, one can lessen the sense of isolation. Existing only as text, a person can become any kind of hero. Such people are often quick, at the slightest provocation, to become the aggressor.

lines.japanese:
同族嫌悪、厭世観……様々な理由があるだろう。
　そしてネットワーク上にも社会がある以上、邪視は存在する。
lines.english: Hatred of one's own kind, misanthropy... Any number of motives may drive them. And wherever society exists—even online—the evil eye exists with it.

lines.japanese:
生身の視線ではなく、無形の悪意としてである。
　文字列に秘められる思想はより極端に肥大し、攻撃的に育つ。
　特定の思想や言葉に対する過剰なアタックを行う。
lines.english: Not as a living gaze, but as disembodied malice. Ideas concealed in strings of text swell to extremes and grow aggressive. They launch disproportionate attacks on particular ideas or words.

lines.japanese: 被害者が加害者になる。
lines.english: The victim becomes the perpetrator.

lines.japanese: 邪な視は交錯し、連鎖となって加速し、インフレーションを起こす。
lines.english: Malevolent gazes intersect, form chains, gather speed, and trigger inflation.

lines.japanese:
体面というものには、対となる反体面なるものが存在する。
　社会的に優れている側に立った際のプライドと、そこから転落もしくは最
初から諸事情により目指さなかった場合の、敵愾心を隠蔽するための仮想矜
持である。
lines.english: Every social face has an opposite: the anti-face. The pride of standing on society's upper tier is matched—when one falls from it, or for whatever reason never aspired to it in the first place—by an imaginary pride used to conceal hostility.

lines.japanese: これらは、まったく病的なものではない。
lines.english: None of this is pathological in the least.

lines.japanese: 大半の人間が属している。
lines.english: Most people belong to one or the other.

lines.japanese:
自らの変性を掲げることに怖じない者のうち、隠す者を侮蔑する人種なら
ば……それは反体面に属することを示す。
lines.english: Among those unafraid to proclaim their own transformation, anyone who scorns those who hide it thereby reveals themselves as belonging to the anti-face.

lines.japanese: 正常。
lines.english: Normal.

lines.japanese: 誰もが差別意識を持つ時代である。
lines.english: It is an age in which everyone harbors prejudice.

lines.japanese:
優劣を競い、知的増税に随伴し損ねた者を攻撃し、一般性を殺傷し、相互
嫌悪の構図を描き上げていく。
lines.english: They vie for superiority, attack those who fail to keep pace with the intellectual tax hike, murder the commonplace, and sketch out a structure of mutual loathing.

lines.japanese:
ネットワーク。網の目。即ち、
　近代社会と呼ばれる、負と憎悪の網―――
lines.english: The network. The mesh. That is to say: the web of negativity and hatred called modern society—

lines.japanese: 社会は必ずしも善に守られてはいないことを認めざるを得ない。
lines.english: We must admit that society is not always protected by goodness.

lines.japanese: 信頼を放棄しなければならない。
lines.english: One must relinquish trust.

lines.japanese: 疑心に陥らねばならない。
lines.english: One must succumb to suspicion.

lines.japanese: 我が身と家族を守るため。
lines.english: To protect oneself and one's family.

lines.japanese: 精神の驕慢さを守るため。
lines.english: To protect the mind's arrogance.

lines.japanese: しかし。
lines.english: But.

lines.japanese:
日中の社会に生きつつ、日常会話なるものを反芻し再生し、内実にまった
く別の論理を走らせる者。
　彼らは一切の矜持なく視線を恐れる。
　恐れて、隠れる。
lines.english: There are those who live in society by day, rehearsing and replaying what passes for ordinary conversation while an entirely different logic runs inside them. They fear the gaze without a shred of pride. Afraid, they hide.

lines.japanese: 隠れて、抱き続ける。
lines.english: Hidden away, they continue to harbor it.

lines.japanese: うち、ごくごく一部が……実行してしまう。
lines.english: Of them, the merest fraction... put it into action.

lines.japanese:
２１世紀初頭、異常殺人は普遍化した。
　どこにでもある、当たり前のこととして認知された。
　理解できない理由で人は殺された。
　不条理が条理に、非常識が常識へと移るのに、１０年かからなかった。
　旧来に多く見られた、幼稚な犯罪も相変わらず多い。
lines.english: At the dawn of the twenty-first century, aberrant murder became commonplace. It came to be seen as an ordinary thing, something that could happen anywhere. People were killed for reasons no one could understand. In less than ten years, the absurd became reason and the unthinkable became common sense. The childish crimes common in earlier times remained as prevalent as ever.

lines.japanese:
だが中には人を慄然とさせる、巧妙かつ残虐なものもあった。
　残虐、と言い切るには少し相違があろう。
　彼らの大半は、残虐ではない。
　むしろ生真面目である。自らの論理には。
lines.english: Some, however, were cunning and savage enough to make people shudder. Though savage may not be precisely the word. Most of these people are not savage. If anything, they are utterly earnest—within the confines of their own logic.

lines.japanese:
そして忠実に人を解体する。何かしらの、尊い理由をもって。
　先天的なものなのか、何らかの原因によってそうなるのか。
lines.english: And faithfully, they dismember people for some reason they hold sacred. Are they born that way, or does some cause make them so?

lines.japanese: いまだ知る者は少ない。
lines.english: Few people yet know.

lines.japanese:
伊月笛子の家の前に、忍は立った。
　さきほどから眩暈が止まらない。
lines.english: Shinobu stood outside Fueko Izuki's house. The dizziness from earlier still would not pass.

lines.japanese:
頭の中で脳を湿らせる液が澱んでいる気がしてな
らない。
lines.english: He could not shake the feeling that the fluid bathing his brain had gone stagnant.

lines.japanese:
明瞭なものが内から浮かび上がらない。
　不満に思うことさえ億劫な有様であり、忍はいま
だインターフォンを鳴らすことはできない。
lines.english: Nothing lucid rose from within him. Even discontent was too much effort. Shinobu still could not ring the intercom.

lines.japanese:
いつまでも、鳴らすことはできない。
　忍は一度たりとて、内側に呼びかけることはでき
なかった。
lines.english: However long he stood there, he could not ring it. Not once had Shinobu managed to call out to those inside.

lines.japanese:
長い幻想が心を蝕むと、やがて忍は時間に属して
いるという事実さえ失う。
lines.english: As the long illusion ate into his mind, even the fact that Shinobu belonged to time eventually slipped away.

lines.japanese:
わずかなずれでも、気付かず歩み続ければいずれ
は逸脱してしまう。
lines.english: Even the slightest deviation, unnoticed and followed long enough, would eventually carry one beyond the path.

lines.japanese:
取って返すことのできない、隔たりを生む。
　心のどこかで自分だけのことではないと思うのだ
が、慰めの断片にさえならない。
lines.english: It creates a distance from which there is no turning back. Somewhere inside, he knows it isn't happening only to him, but the thought offers not even a fragment of comfort.

lines.japanese:
血気盛んな子供はいかにして死ぬのか考える。
　そう、高木に登った時に死ぬのだ。
　彼はその瞬間、孤立を知る。
lines.english: Consider how a reckless child dies. Yes: he dies when he climbs a tall tree. In that instant, he discovers isolation.

lines.japanese:
もう自力では降りることはできない。
　幹にしがみつく力もいつかは尽きる。
　近くに大人はいない。同じ高さに大人はいない。
lines.english: He can no longer climb down under his own power. Eventually, his strength to cling to the trunk will fail. There are no adults nearby. No adults at his height.

lines.japanese:
下方に肉親が立つかも知れない。
　だがその愛すべき家族さえ、今の自分を助けるこ
とはできない。
lines.english: His family may be standing below. But even that beloved family cannot save him now.

lines.japanese: 絶対の孤独。
lines.english: Absolute solitude.

lines.japanese:
高く登りすぎてクレーン車を持ってしても、助か
る見込みがないと判明した瞬間、彼は夕空を感情に
染まらない顔で眺めて惚けることを選ぶ。
lines.english: Once he realizes he has climbed too high for even a crane to save him, he chooses to stare at the evening sky and drift into vacancy, his face untouched by emotion.

lines.japanese:
落ちて死ぬために。
　親しい友や親兄弟に見守られながら、心のどこか
では彼らと同じ高さに還るのだと欺瞞し、手を放す。
lines.english: In order to fall and die. Watched by close friends, parents, and siblings, he lets go, deceiving himself somewhere in his heart that he is returning to their height.

lines.japanese:
大地に横たわる歪んだカラダを、大人たちは声も
なく囲む。
lines.english: The adults gather in silence around the twisted body lying on the earth.

lines.japanese:
誰が何を定義できるのだろう。
　まず誰から口を開くべきなのだろう。
　親はもう壊れた。
lines.english: Who can define anything? Who should be the first to speak? The parent is already broken.

lines.japanese:
言葉を失い、心を失う。
　子に同調しすぎたが故に、そうなった。
　悲鳴のない喪失。
lines.english: Words gone. Mind gone. It happened because the parent had synchronized too closely with the child. A loss without a scream.

lines.japanese:
きっかけもなく、慰めの言葉もない。
　子の姉はその時、気付いていた。
lines.english: There is no trigger, and no word of comfort. At that moment, the child's older sister realized

lines.japanese:
彼ら三人の心が、今この場において同期していた
ことを。
lines.english: that the minds of all three were synchronized here and now.

lines.japanese:
落下した子の肉体だけが、まだ生命の灯を残して
いることを知った。
lines.english: She knew that only the fallen child's body still held the flame of life.

lines.japanese:
やがて救急車が来るだろう。
　だから母親同様に黙っていた。
　全員が、無言のままそのときを待った。
lines.english: An ambulance would come eventually. And so, like her mother, she kept silent. All of them waited in silence for that moment.

lines.japanese: いつまでも、いつまでも―――
lines.english: Forever and ever—
“...Shino.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえ、知っているんだろ？」
lines.english: “You know, don't you?”

lines.japanese: 「……何をだい」
lines.english: “...Know what?”

lines.japanese: 「伊月笛子のこと」
lines.english: “About Fueko Izuki.”

lines.japanese: 「やはり、知っていたな」
lines.english: “I thought so. You knew.”

lines.japanese:
こんな時、うまく回らない舌を忍は恨めしく思う。
　沈黙があまりにも多弁すぎて。
lines.english: At moments like this, Shinobu resented his tongue for refusing to move. His silence was far too eloquent.

lines.japanese: 「……伊月笛子……あいつは」
lines.english: “...Fueko Izuki... she's—”

lines.japanese: 「人殺しだ」
lines.english: “She's a killer.”

lines.japanese:
やがて覚悟を決めた忍の口から、煮凝りのような
問いかけが発せられた。
lines.english: When Shinobu finally steeled himself, the question left his mouth like a lump of aspic.

lines.japanese: 「……どういう縁でそれを？」
lines.english: “...How did you find out?”

lines.japanese: 「やっぱり例の探偵さん？」
lines.english: “That detective again?”
“...Yeah.”

lines.japanese: 「といっても、調べたのはオレさ」
lines.english: “Though I was the one who looked into it.”

lines.japanese: 「例の件」
lines.english: “That case.”

lines.japanese: ぴしり、と章二の言葉が宙に鞭を打つ。
lines.english: Shouji's words cracked like a whip through the air.
“That case...?”

lines.japanese: 「とぼけるなよ」
lines.english: “Don't play dumb.”

lines.japanese: 「連続猟奇殺人犯だ」
lines.english: “The serial killer behind those bizarre murders.”

lines.japanese: 「その言葉も、いい加減なこじつけだと僕は思うよ」
lines.english: “I think even that label is a pretty arbitrary stretch.”

lines.japanese:
「前におまえらが言っていたことがあったろ？
　気配を消して透明人間になるってやつだ」
lines.english: “Remember what you were saying before? About erasing your presence and becoming invisible.”

lines.japanese:
「オレなりにいろいろと気になるところがあって、
　ほうぼう回って調べてみた」
lines.english: “I had a few questions of my own, so I went around and did some investigating.”

lines.japanese:
「……そのうちの一つにな、とんでもないレアなも
　のがあった」
lines.english: “...And one of the things I turned up was something you almost never hear.”

lines.japanese: 「警察の捜査資料でも？」
lines.english: “Police records?”

lines.japanese:
揶揄するような言葉は、この出来事に警察が何の
力も持っていないことを示すものだった。
lines.english: The mocking question made clear that the police had no power over this affair.

lines.japanese: 章二は冷静に言葉を返した。
lines.english: Shouji answered calmly.

lines.japanese: 「書類じゃない。噂だ」
lines.english: “Not records. A rumor.”

lines.japanese:
「……おびただしい数を殺してる。もうずいぶん前の
　ことだ」
lines.english: “...She killed a huge number of people. It was a long time ago.”

lines.japanese: 「学校帰りに繁華街に寄ったことがあるそうだ」
lines.english: “Apparently she stopped in the entertainment district on her way home from school.”

lines.japanese:
「そのとき、まあお決まりだが……あの目立つ制服
　は狙われた」
lines.english: “And then, as you'd expect... that conspicuous uniform made her a target.”

lines.japanese:
「路地裏に連れ込まれて、誰も助ける者はいなかっ
　た。そういうものだ。別に道ばたで衣服を剥ぎ取っ
　てるわけじゃないからな」
lines.english: “They dragged her into an alley, and nobody helped. That's how these things go. It wasn't as if they were stripping off her clothes in the middle of the street.”

lines.japanese: 「多少強引なナンパって風に解釈されることもある」
lines.english: “People can write it off as nothing more than aggressive flirting.”

lines.japanese: 「このときもそうだった」
lines.english: “That's what happened then, too.”

lines.japanese:
「そして……どういう方法でかは知らないが、殺し
　た―――」
lines.english: “And then... I don't know how she did it, but she killed them—”

lines.japanese: 伊月笛子の殺傷。
lines.english: Fueko Izuki's lethal violence.

lines.english: (What... was that?)

lines.english: The sight of Fueko Izuki's lethal violence.
